hexagrams.name: 乾
hexagrams.guaCi: 乾，元享利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天行健，君子以自強不息。

lines.ci: 初九，潛龍勿用。
lines.ciEn: In the first (or lowest) NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon lying hid (in the deep). It is not the time for active doing.

lines.ci: 九二，見龍在田，利見大人。
lines.ciEn: In the second NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon appearing in the field. It will be advantageous to meet with the great man.

lines.ci: 九三，君子終日乾乾，夕惕若，厲，無咎。
lines.ciEn: In the third NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the superior man active and vigilant all the day, and in the evening still careful and apprehensive. (The position is) dangerous, but there will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 九四，或躍在淵，無咎。
lines.ciEn: In the fourth NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as the dragon looking) as if he were leaping up, but still in the deep. There will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 九五，飛龍在天，利見大人。
lines.ciEn: In the fifth NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon on the wing in the sky. It will be advantageous to meet with the great man.

lines.ci: 上九，亢龍有悔。
lines.ciEn: In the sixth (or topmost) NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon exceeding the proper limits. There will be occasion for repentance. 7. (The lines of this hexagram are all strong and undivided, as appears from) the use of the number NINE. If the host of dragons (thus) appearing were to divest themselves of their heads, there would be good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Khien (represents) what is great and originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and firm.
hexagrams.xiangEn: Heaven, in its motion, (gives the idea of) strength. The superior man, in accordance with this, nerves himself to ceaseless activity.

hexagrams.name: 坤
hexagrams.guaCi: 坤，元亨，利牝馬之貞。君子有攸往，先迷，後得，主利。西南得朋，東北喪朋，安貞吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：地勢坤，君子以厚德載物。

lines.ci: 初六，履霜，堅冰至。
lines.ciEn: In the first SIX, divided, (we see its subject) treading on hoarfrost. The strong ice will come (by and by).

lines.ci: 六二，直方大。不習無不利。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, (shows the attribute of) being straight, square, and great. (Its operation), without repeated efforts, will be in every respect advantageous.

lines.ci: 六三，含章可貞。或從王事，無成有終。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, (shows its subject) keeping his excellence under restraint, but firmly maintaining it. If he should have occasion to engage in the king's service, though he will not claim the success (for himself), he will bring affairs to a good issue.

lines.ci: 六四，括囊，無咎，無譽。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, (shows the symbol of) a sack tied up. There will be no ground for blame or for praise.

lines.ci: 六五，黃裳，元吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, (shows) the yellow lower garment. There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，龍戰於野，其血玄黃。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided (shows) dragons fighting in the wild. Their blood is purple and yellow. 7. (The lines of this hexagram are all weak and divided, as appears from) the use of the number six. If those (who are thus represented) be perpetually correct and firm, advantage will arise.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Khwăn (represents) what is great and originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and having the firmness of a mare. When the superior man (hereintended) has to make any movement, if he take the initiative, he will go astray; if he follow, he will find his (proper) lord. The advantageousness will be seen in his getting friends in the south-west, and losing friends in the north-east. If he rest in correctness and firmness, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.xiangEn: The (capacity and sustaining) power of the earth is what is denoted by Kun. The superior man, in accordance with this, with his large virtue supports (men and) things.

hexagrams.name: 屯
hexagrams.guaCi: 屯，元亨利貞。勿用有攸往，利建侯。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雲雷，屯。君子以經綸。

lines.ci: 初九，盤桓，利居貞，利建侯。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows the difficulty (its subject has) in advancing. It will be advantageous for him to abide correct and firm; advantageous (also) to be made a feudal ruler.

lines.ci: 六二，屯如邅如，乘馬班加。匪寇婚媾，女子貞不字，十年乃字。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows (its subject) distressed and obliged to return; (even) the horses of her chariot (also) seem to be retreating. (But) not by a spoiler (is she assailed), but by one who seeks her to be his wife. The young lady maintains her firm correctness, and declines a union. After ten years she will be united, and have children.

lines.ci: 六三，即鹿無虞，惟入於林中，君子幾，不如舍，往吝。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one following the deer without (the guidance of) the forester, and only finding himself in the midst of the forest. The superior man, acquainted with the secret risks, thinks it better to give up the chase. If he went forward, he would regret it.

lines.ci: 六四，乘馬班如，求婚媾，往吉，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows (its subject as a lady), the horses of whose chariot appear in retreat. She seeks, however, (the help of) him who seeks her to be his wife. Advance will be fortunate; all will turn out advantageously.

lines.ci: 九五，屯其膏，小貞吉，大貞凶。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the difficulties in the way of (its subject's) dispensing the rich favours that might be expected from him. With firmness and correctness there will be good fortune in small things; (even) with them in great things there will be evil.

lines.ci: 上六，乘馬班如，泣血漣如。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows (its subject) with the horses of his chariot obliged to retreat, and weeping tears of blood in streams.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kun (indicates that in the case which it presupposes) there will be great progress and success, and the advantage will come from being correct and firm. (But) any movement in advance should not be (lightly) undertaken. There will be advantage in appointing feudal princes.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) clouds and (that representing) thunder form Zhun. The superior man, in accordance with this, (adjusts his measures of government) as in sorting the threads of the warp and woof.

hexagrams.name: 蒙
hexagrams.guaCi: 蒙，亨。匪我求童蒙，童蒙求我。初筮告，再三瀆，瀆則不告，利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山下出泉，蒙。君子以果行育德。

lines.ci: 初六，發蒙，利用刑人，用說桎梏，以往吝。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, (has respect to) the dispelling of ignorance. It will be advantageous to use punishment (for that purpose), and to remove the shackles (from the mind). But going on in that way (of punishment) will give occasion for regret.

lines.ci: 九二，包蒙，吉。納婦吉，子克家。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) exercising forbearance with the ignorant, in which there will be good fortune; and admitting (even the goodness of women, which will also be fortunate. (He may be described also as) a son able to (sustain the burden of) his family.

lines.ci: 六三，勿用娶女，見金夫，不有躬，無攸利。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, (seems to say) that one should not marry a woman whose emblem it might be, for that, when she sees a man of wealth, she will not keep her person from him, and in no wise will advantage come from her.

lines.ci: 六四，困蒙，吝。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, (shows its subject as if) bound in chains of ignorance. There will be occasion for regret.

lines.ci: 六五，童蒙，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject as a simple lad without experience. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，擊蒙，不利為寇，利禦寇。
lines.ciEn: In the topmost NINE, undivided, we see one smiting the ignorant (youth). But no advantage will come from doing him an injury. Advantage would come from warding off injury from him.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Măng (indicates that in the case which it presupposes) there will be progress and success. I do not (go and) seek the youthful and inexperienced,but he comes and seeks me. When he shows (the sincerity that marks) the first recourse to divination, I instruct him. If he apply a second and third time, that is troublesome; and I do not instruct the troublesome. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and beneath it that for a spring issuing forth form Meng. The superior man, in accordance with this, strives to be resolute in his conduct and nourishes his virtue.

hexagrams.name: 需
hexagrams.guaCi: 需，有孚，光亨，貞吉。利涉大川。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雲上於天，需。君子以飲食宴樂。

lines.ci: 初九，需於郊，利用恆，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject waiting in the distant border. It will be well for him constantly to maintain (the purpose thus shown), in which case there will be no error.

lines.ci: 九二，需於沙，小有言，終吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject waiting on the sand (of the mountain stream). He will (suffer) the small (injury of) being spoken (against), but in the end there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，需於泥，致寇至。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject in the mud (close by the stream). He thereby invites the approach of injury.

lines.ci: 六四，需於血，出自穴。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject waiting in (the place of) blood. But he will get out of the cavern.

lines.ci: 九五，需於酒食，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject waiting amidst the appliances of a feast. Through his firmness and correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，入於穴，有不速之客三人來，敬之終吉。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject entered into the cavern. (But) there are three guests coming, without being urged, (to his help). If he receive them respectfully, there will be good fortune in the end.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Hsü intimates that, with the sincerity which is declared in it, there will be brilliant success. With firmness there will be good fortune; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for) clouds ascending over that for the sky forms Xu. The superior man, in accordance with this, eats and drinks, feasts and enjoys himself (as if there were nothing else to employ him).

hexagrams.name: 讼
hexagrams.guaCi: 訟，有孚，窒惕，中吉，終凶。利見大人，不利涉大川。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天與水違行，訟。君子以作事謀始。

lines.ci: 初六，不永所事，小有言，終吉。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject not perpetuating the matter about which (the contention is). He will suffer the small (injury) of being spoken against, but the end will be fortunate.

lines.ci: 九二，不克訟，歸而逋。其邑人三百戶，無眚。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject unequal to the contention. If he retire and keep concealed (where) the inhabitants of his city are (only) three hundred families, he will fall into no mistake.

lines.ci: 六三，食舊德，貞厲，終吉。或從王事，無成。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping in the old place assigned for his support, and firmly correct. Perilous as the position is, there will be good fortune in the end. Should he perchance engage in the king's business, he will not (claim the merit of) achievement.

lines.ci: 九四，不克訟，復即命渝，安貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject unequal to the contention. He returns to (the study of Heaven's) ordinances, changes (his wish to contend), and rests in being firm and correct. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九五，訟，元吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contending - and with great good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，或錫之鞶帶，終朝三褫之。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how its subject may have the leathern belt conferred on him (by the sovereign), and thrice it shall be taken from him in a morning.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Sung intimates how, though there is sincerity in one's contention, he will yet meet with opposition and obstruction; but if he cherish an apprehensive caution, there will be good fortune, while, if he must prosecute the contention to the (bitter) end, there will be evil. It will be advantageous to see the great man; it will not be advantageous to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) heaven and (that representing) water, moving away from each other, form Song. The superior man, in accordance with this, in the transaction of affairs takes good counsel about his first steps.

hexagrams.name: 师
hexagrams.guaCi: 師貞，丈人吉，無咎。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：地中有水，師。君子以容民畜眾。

lines.ci: 初六，師出以律，否臧凶。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows the host going forth according to the rules (for such a movement). If these be not good, there will be evil.

lines.ci: 九二，在師中，吉，無咎。王三錫命。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows (the leader) in the midst of the host. There will be good fortune and no error. The king has thrice conveyed to him the orders (of his favour).

lines.ci: 六三，師或輿屍，凶。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows how the host may, possibly, have many inefficient leaders. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 六四，師左次，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the host in retreat. There is no error.

lines.ci: 六五，田有禽，利執言，無咎。長子帥師，弟子輿屍，貞凶。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows birds in the fields, which it will be advantageous to seize (and destroy). In that case there will be no error. If the oldest son leads the host, and younger men (idly occupy offices assigned to them), however firm and correct he may be, there will be evil.

lines.ci: 上六，大君有命，開國承家，小人勿用。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows the great ruler delivering his charges, (appointing some) to be rulers of states, and others to undertake the headship of clans; but small men should not be employed (in such positions).

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Sze indicates how, in the case which it supposes, with firmness and correctness, and (a leader of) age and experience, there will be good fortune and no error.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the earth and in the midst of it that representing water, form Shi. The superior man, in accordance with this, nourishes and educates the people, and collects (from among them) the multitudes (of the hosts).

hexagrams.name: 比
hexagrams.guaCi: 比吉。原筮元永貞，無咎。不寧方來，後夫凶。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：地上有水，比。先王以建萬國，親諸侯。

lines.ci: 初六，有孚比之，無咎。有孚盈缶，終來有它吉。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject seeking by his sincerity to win the attachment of his object. There will be no error. Let (the breast) be full of sincerity as an earthenware vessel is of its contents, and it will in the end bring other advantages.

lines.ci: 六二，比之自內，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: In the second SIX, divided, we see the movement towards union and attachment proceeding from the inward (mind). With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，比之匪人。
lines.ciEn: In the third SIX, divided, we see its subject seeking for union with such as ought not to be associated with.

lines.ci: 六四，外比之，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: In the fourth SIX, divided, we see its subject seeking for union with the one beyond himself. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九五，顯比。王用三驅，失前禽，邑人不誡，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, affords the most illustrious instance of seeking union and attachment. (We seem to see in it) the king urging his pursuit of the game (only) in three directions, and allowing the escape of all the animals before him, while the people of his towns do not warn one another (to prevent it). There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，比之無首，凶。
lines.ciEn: In the topmost SIX, divided, we see one seeking union and attachment without having taken the first step (to such an end). There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Pî indicates that (under the conditions which it supposes) there is good fortune. But let (the principal party intended in it) re-examine himself, (as if)by divination, whether his virtue be great, unintermitting, and firm. If it be so, there will be no error. Those who have not rest will then come to him; and with those who are (too) late in coming it will be ill.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the earth, and over it (that representing) water, form Bi. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, established the various states and maintained an affectionate relation to their princes.

hexagrams.name: 小畜
hexagrams.guaCi: 小畜，亨。密雲不雨，自我西郊。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：風行天上，小畜。君子以懿文德。

lines.ci: 初九，復自道，何其咎，吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject returning and pursuing his own course. What mistake should he fall into? There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九二，牽復，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject, by the attraction (of the former line), returning (to the proper course). There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，輿說輻，夫妻反目。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a carriage, the strap beneath which has been removed, or of a husband and wife looking on each other with averted eyes.

lines.ci: 六四，有孚，血去惕出，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity. The danger of bloodshed is thereby averted, and his (ground for) apprehension dismissed. There will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 九五，有孚攣如，富以其鄰。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity, and drawing others to unite with him. Rich in resources, he employs his neighbours (in the same cause with himself).

lines.ci: 上九，既雨既處，尚得載，婦貞厲。月幾望，君子徵凶。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how the rain has fallen, and the (onward progress) is stayed;--(so) must we value the full accumulation of the virtue (represented by the upper trigram). But a wife (exercising restraint), however firm and correct she may be, is in a position of peril, (and like) the moon approaching to the full. If the superior man prosecute his measures (in such circumstances), there will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Hsiâo Khû indicates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. (We see) dense clouds, but no rain coming from our borders in the west.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the sky, and that representing wind moving above it, form Xiao Xu The superior man, in accordance with this, adorns the outward manifestation of his virtue.

hexagrams.name: 履
hexagrams.guaCi: 履虎尾，不咥人。亨。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：上天下澤，履。君子以辯上下，定民志。

lines.ci: 初九，素履，往無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading his accustomed path. If he go forward, there will be no error.

lines.ci: 九二，履道坦坦，幽人貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading the path that is level and easy;--a quiet and solitary man, to whom, if he be firm and correct, there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，眇能視，跛能履，履虎尾，咥人，凶。武人為於大君。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows a one-eyed man (who thinks he) can see; a lame man (who thinks he) can walk well; one who treads on the tail of a tiger and is bitten. (All this indicates) ill fortune. We have a (mere) bravo acting the part of a great ruler.

lines.ci: 九四，履虎尾，愬愬，終吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading on the tail of a tiger. He becomes full of apprehensive caution, and in the end there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九五，夬履，貞厲。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the resolute tread of its subject. Though he be firm and correct, there will be peril.

lines.ci: 上九，視履考祥，其旋元吉。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, tells us to look at (the whole course) that is trodden, and examine the presage which that gives. If it be complete and without failure, there will be great good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: (Lî suggests the idea of) one treading on the tail of a tiger, which does not bite him. There will be progress and success.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the sky above, and below it (that representing the waters of) a marsh, form Lu. The superior man, in accordance with this, discriminates between high and low, and gives settlement to the aims of the people.

hexagrams.name: 泰
hexagrams.guaCi: 泰，小往大來，吉，亨。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天地交泰，後以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。

lines.ci: 初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，徵吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of grass pulled up, and bringing with it other stalks with whose roots it is connected. Advance (on the part of its subject) will be fortunate.

lines.ci: 九二，包荒，用馮河，不遐遺。朋亡，得尚於中行。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows one who can bear with the uncultivated, will cross the Ho without a boat, does not forget the distant, and has no (selfish) friendships. Thus does he prove himself acting in accordance with the course of the due Mean.

lines.ci: 九三，無平不陂，無往不復。艱貞無咎。勿恤其孚，於食有福。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows that, while there is no state of peace that is not liable to be disturbed, and no departure (of evil men) so that they shall not return, yet when one is firm and correct, as he realises the distresses that may arise, he will commit no error. There is no occasion for sadness at the certainty (of such recurring changes); and in this mood the happiness (of the present) may be (long) enjoyed.

lines.ci: 六四，翩翩，不富以其鄰，不戒以孚。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject fluttering (down);--not relying on his own rich resources, but calling in his neighbours. (They all come) not as having received warning, but in the sincerity (of their hearts).

lines.ci: 六五，帝乙歸妹，以祉元吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth six, divided, reminds us of (king) Tî-yî's (rule about the) marriage of his younger sister. By such a course there is happiness and there will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，城復於隍，勿用師，自邑告命，貞吝。
lines.ciEn: The sixth six, divided, shows us the city wall returned into the moat. It is not the time to use the army. (The subject of the line) may, indeed, announce his orders to the people of his own city; but however correct and firm he may be, he will have cause for regret.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In Thâi (we see) the little gone and the great come. (It indicates that) there will be good fortune, with progress and success.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams for) heaven and earth in communication together form Tai. The (sage) sovereign, in harmony with this, fashions and completes (his regulations) after the courses of heaven and earth, and assists the application of the adaptations furnished by them, - in order to benefit the people.

hexagrams.name: 否
hexagrams.guaCi: 否之匪人，不利君子貞，大往小來。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天地不交，否。君子以儉德闢難，不可榮以祿。

lines.ci: 初六，拔茅茹以其彙，貞吉，亨。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, suggests the idea of grass pulled up, and bringing with it other stalks with whose roots it is connected. With firm correctness (on the part of its subject), there will be good fortune and progress.

lines.ci: 六二，包承，小人吉，大人否，亨。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject patient and obedient. To the small man (comporting himself so) there will be good fortune. If the great man (comport himself) as the distress and obstruction require, he will have success.

lines.ci: 六三，包羞。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject ashamed of the purpose folded (in his breast).

lines.ci: 九四，有命，無咎，疇離祉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject acting in accordance with the ordination (of Heaven), and committing no error. His companions will come and share in his happiness.

lines.ci: 九五，休否，大人吉。其亡其亡，繫於包桑。
lines.ciEn: In the fifth NINE, undivided, we see him who brings the distress and obstruction to a close,--the great man and fortunate. (But let him say), 'We may perish! We may perish!' (so shall the state of things become firm, as if) bound to a clump of bushy mulberry trees.

lines.ci: 上九，傾否，先否後喜。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the overthrow (and removal of) the condition of distress and obstruction. Before this there was that condition. Hereafter there will be joy.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In Phî there is the want of good understanding between the (different classes of) men, and its indication is unfavourable to the firm and correct course of the superior man. We see in it the great gone and the little come.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams of) heaven and earth, not in intercommunication, form Pi. The superior man, in accordance with this, restrains (the manifestation) of) his virtue, and avoids the calamities (that threaten him). There is no opportunity of conferring on him the glory of emolument.

hexagrams.name: 同人
hexagrams.guaCi: 同人於野，亨。利涉大川，利君子貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天與火，同人。君子以類族辯物。

lines.ci: 初九，同人於門，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men just issuing from his gate. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六二，同人於宗，吝。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in relation with his kindred. There will be occasion for regret.

lines.ci: 九三，伏戎於莽，升其高陵，三歲不興。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) with his arms hidden in the thick grass, and at the top of a high mound. (But) for three years he makes no demonstration.

lines.ci: 九四，乘其墉，弗克攻，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) mounted on the city wall; but he does not proceed to make the attack (he contemplates). There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九五，同人先號咷而後笑，大師克相遇。
lines.ciEn: In the fifth NINE, undivided, (the representative of) the union of men first wails and cries out, and then laughs. His great host conquers, and he (and the subject of the second line) meet together.

lines.ci: 上九，同人於郊，無悔。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in the suburbs. There will be no occasion for repentance.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Thung Zăn (or 'Union of men') appears here (as we find it) in the (remote districts of the) country, indicating progress and success. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to maintain the firm correctness of the superior man.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams for) heaven and fire form Tong Ren. The superior man, in accordance with this), distinguishes things according to their kinds and classes.

hexagrams.name: 大有
hexagrams.guaCi: 大有，元亨。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：火在天上，大有。君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。

lines.ci: 初九：無交害，匪咎，艱則無咎。
lines.ciEn: In the first NINE, undivided, there is no approach to what is injurious, and there is no error. Let there be a realisation of the difficulty (and danger of the position), and there will be no error (to the end).

lines.ci: 九二：大車以載，有攸往，無咎。
lines.ciEn: In the second NINE, undivided, we have a large waggon with its load. In whatever direction advance is made, there will be no error.

lines.ci: 九三：公用亨於天子，小人弗克。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows us a feudal prince presenting his offerings to the Son of Heaven. A small man would be unequal (to such a duty).

lines.ci: 九四，匪其彭，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject keeping his great resources under restraint. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六五：厥孚交如，威如吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows the sincerity of its subject reciprocated by that of all the others (represented in the hexagram). Let him display a proper majesty, and there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九：自天祐之，吉，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject with help accorded to him from Heaven. There will be good fortune, advantage in every respect.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Tâ Yû indicates that, (under the circumstances which it implies), there will be great progress and success.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for) heaven and (that of) fire above it form Da You. The superior man, in accordance with this, represses what is evil and gives distinction to what is good, in sympathy with the excellent Heaven-conferred (nature).。

hexagrams.name: 谦
hexagrams.guaCi: 謙，亨。君子有終。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：地中有山，謙。君子以裒多益寡，稱物平施。

lines.ci: 初六，謙謙君子，用涉大川，吉。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows us the superior man who adds humility to humility. (Even) the great stream may be crossed with this, and there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六二，鳴謙，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows us humility that has made itself recognised. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，勞謙，君子有終，吉。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows the superior man of (acknowledged) merit. He will maintain his success to the end, and have good fortune.

lines.ci: 六四，無不利，撝謙。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one, whose action would be in every way advantageous, stirring up (the more) his humility.

lines.ci: 六五，不富以其鄰，利用侵伐，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one who, without being rich, is able to employ his neighbours. He may advantageously use the force of arms. All his movements will be advantageous.

lines.ci: 上六，鳴謙，利用行師，徵邑國。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows us humility that has made itself recognised. The subject of it will with advantage put his hosts in motion; but (he will only) punish his own towns and state.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Khien indicates progress and success. The superior man, (being humble as it implies), will have a (good) issue (to his undertakings).
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for) the earth and (that of) a mountain in the midst of it form Qian. The superior man, in accordance with this, diminishes what is excessive (in himself), and increases where there is any defect, bringing about an equality, according to the nature of the case, in his treatment (of himself and others).

hexagrams.name: 豫
hexagrams.guaCi: 豫，利建侯、行師。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

lines.ci: 初六，鳴豫，凶。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject proclaiming his pleasure and satisfaction. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 六二，介於石，不終日，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one who is firm as a rock. (He sees a thing) without waiting till it has come to pass; with his firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，盱豫悔，遲有悔。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking up (for favours), while he indulges the feeling of pleasure and satisfaction. If he would understand!--If he be late in doing so, there will indeed be occasion for repentance.

lines.ci: 九四，由豫，大有得，勿疑，朋盍簮。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom the harmony and satisfaction come. Great is the success which he obtains. Let him not allow suspicions to enter his mind, and thus friends will gather around him.

lines.ci: 六五：貞疾，恆不死。
lines.ciEn: The fifth six, divided, shows one with a chronic complaint, but who lives on without dying.

lines.ci: 上六，冥豫，成有渝，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The topmost six, divided, shows its subject with darkened mind devoted to the pleasure and satisfaction (of the time); but if he change his course even when (it may be considered as) completed, there will be no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Yü indicates that, (in the state which it implies), feudal princes may be set up, and the hosts put in motion, with advantage.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams for) the earth and thunder issuing from it with its crashing noise form Yu. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, composed their music and did honour to virtue, presenting it especially and most grandly to God, when they associated with Him (at the service) their highest ancestor and their father.

hexagrams.name: 随
hexagrams.guaCi: 隨，元亨利貞，無咎。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤中有雷，隨。君子以嚮晦入宴息。

lines.ci: 初九，官有渝，貞吉。出門交有功。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows us one changing the object of his pursuit; but if he be firm and correct, there will he good fortune. Going beyond (his own) gate to find associates, he will achieve merit.

lines.ci: 六二，係小子，失丈夫。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the little boy, and lets go the man of age and experience.

lines.ci: 六三，係丈夫，失小子，隨有求，得。利居貞。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the man of age and experience, and lets go. the little boy. Such following will get what it seeks; but it will be advantageous to adhere to what is firm and correct.

lines.ci: 九四，隨有獲，貞凶。有孚在道，以明，何咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows us one followed and obtaining (adherents). Though he be firm and correct, there will be evil. If he be sincere (however) in his course, and make that evident, into what error will he fall?

lines.ci: 九五：孚於嘉吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows us (the ruler) sincere in (fostering all) that is excellent. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六：拘係之，乃從維之。王用亨於西山。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows us (that sincerity) firmly held and clung to, yea, and bound fast. (We see) the king with it presenting his offerings on the western mountain.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Sui indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. There will (then) be no error.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for the waters of) a marsh and (that for) thunder (hidden) in the midst of it form Sui. The superior man in accordance with this, when it is getting towards dark, enters (his house) and rests.

hexagrams.name: 蛊
hexagrams.guaCi: 蠱，元亨。利涉大川。先甲三日，後甲三日。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山下有風，蠱。君子以振民育德。

lines.ci: 初六，乾父之蠱，有子考，無咎。厲，終吉。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. If he be an (able) son, the father will escape the blame of having erred. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune in the end.

lines.ci: 九二，乾母之蠱，不可貞。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his mother. He should not (carry) his firm correctness (to the utmost).

lines.ci: 九三，乾父之蠱，小有悔，無大咎。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. There may be some small occasion for repentance, but there will not be any great error.

lines.ci: 六四，裕父之蠱，往見吝。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows (a son) viewing indulgently the troubles caused by his father. If he go forward, he will find cause to regret it.

lines.ci: 六五，乾父之蠱，用譽。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. He obtains the praise of using (the fit instrument for his work).

lines.ci: 上九，不事王侯，高尚其事。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows us one who does not serve either king or feudal lord, but in a lofty spirit prefers (to attend to) his own affairs.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kû indicates great progress and success (to him who deals properly with the condition represented by it). There will be advantage in (efforts like that of) crossing the great stream. (He should weigh well, however, the events of) three days before the turning point, and those (to be done) three days after it.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for) a mountain, and below it that for wind, form Gu. The superior man, in accordance with this, (addresses himself to) help the people and nourish his own virtue.

hexagrams.name: 临
hexagrams.guaCi: 臨，元亨利貞。至於八月有凶。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤上有地，臨。君子以教思無窮，容保民無疆。

lines.ci: 初九，咸臨，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing in company (with the subject of the second line). Through his firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九二，咸臨，吉，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing in company (with the subject of the first line). There will be good fortune; (advancing) will be in every way advantageous.

lines.ci: 六三，甘臨，無攸利，既憂之，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one well pleased (indeed) to advance, (but whose action) will be in no way advantageous. If he become anxious about it (however), there will be no error.

lines.ci: 六四，至臨，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one advancing in the highest mode. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六五，知臨，大君之宜，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows the advance of wisdom, such as befits the great ruler. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，敦臨，吉，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the advance of honesty and generosity. There will be good fortune, and no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Lin (indicates that under the conditions supposed in it) there will be great progress and success, while it will be advantageous to be firmly correct. In the eighth month there will be evil.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for) the waters of a marsh and that for the earth above it form Lin. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his purposes of instruction that are inexhaustible, and nourishes and supports the people without limit.

hexagrams.name: 观
hexagrams.guaCi: 觀，盥而不薦，有孚顒若。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：風行地上，觀。先王以省方觀民設教。

lines.ci: 初六，童觀，小人無咎，君子吝。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows the looking of a lad;--not blamable in men of inferior rank, but matter for regret in superior men.

lines.ci: 六二，闚觀，利女貞。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one peeping out from a door. It would be advantageous if it were (merely) the firm correctness of a female.

lines.ci: 六三，觀我生，進退。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking at (the course of) his own life, to advance or recede (accordingly).

lines.ci: 六四：觀國之光，利用賓於王。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one contemplating the glory of the kingdom. It will be advantageous for him, being such as he is, (to seek) to be a guest of the king.

lines.ci: 九五：觀我生，君子無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his own life(-course). A superior man, he will (thus) fall into no error.

lines.ci: 上九，觀其生，君子無咎。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his character to see if it be indeed that of a superior man. He will not fall into error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kwân shows (how he whom it represents should be like) the worshipper who has washed his hands, but not (yet) presented his offerings;--with sincerity and an appearance of dignity (commanding reverent regard).
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the earth, and that for wind moving above it, form Guan. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, examined the (different) regions (of the kingdom), to see the (ways of the) people, and set forth their instructions.

hexagrams.name: 噬嗑
hexagrams.guaCi: 噬嗑，享，利用獄。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷電，噬嗑。先王以明罰勑法。

lines.ci: 初九，屨校滅趾，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows one with his feet in the stocks and deprived of his toes. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六二，噬膚滅鼻，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one biting through the soft flesh, and (going on to) bite off the nose. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六三，噬腊肉，遇毒，小吝，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one gnawing dried flesh, and meeting with what is disagreeable. There will be occasion for some small regret, but no (great) error.

lines.ci: 九四，噬乾胏，得金矢，利艱貞，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows one gnawing the flesh dried on the bone, and getting the pledges of money and arrows. It will be advantageous to him to realise the difficulty of his task and be firm,--in which case there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六五，噬乾肉，得黃金，貞厲，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one gnawing at dried flesh, and finding the yellow gold. Let him be firm and correct, realising the peril (of his position). There will be no error.

lines.ci: 上九，何校滅耳，凶。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows one wearing the cangue, and deprived of his cars. There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Shih Ho indicates successful progress (in the condition of things which it supposes). It will be advantageous to use legal constraints.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams representing) thunder and lightning form Shi He. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, framed their penalties with intelligence, and promulgated their laws

hexagrams.name: 贲
hexagrams.guaCi: 賁，亨。小利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山下有火，賁。君子以明庶政，無敢折獄。

lines.ci: 初九：賁其趾，舍車而徒。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows one adorning (the way of) his feet. He can discard a carriage and walk on foot.

lines.ci: 六二：賁其須。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one adorning his beard.

lines.ci: 九三：賁如濡如，永貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of being adorned and bedewed (with rich favours). But let him ever maintain his firm correctness, and there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六四：賁如皤如，白馬翰如，匪寇婚媾。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one looking as if adorned, but only in white. As if (mounted on) a white horse, and furnished with wings, (he seeks union with the subject of the first line), while (the intervening third pursues), not as a robber, but intent on a matrimonial alliance.

lines.ci: 六五：賁於丘園，束帛戔戔，吝。終吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject adorned by (the occupants of) the heights and gardens. He bears his roll of silk, small and slight. He may appear stingy; but there will be good fortune in the end.

lines.ci: 上九：白賁，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows one with white as his (only) ornament. There will be no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Pî indicates that there should be free course (in what it denotes). There will be little advantage (however) if it be allowed to advance (and take the lead).
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain and that for fire under it form Bi. The superior man, in accordance with this, throws a brilliancy around his various processes of government, but does not dare (in a similar way) to decide cases of criminal litigation.

hexagrams.name: 剥
hexagrams.guaCi: 剝，不利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山附於地，剝。上以厚下安宅。

lines.ci: 初六，剝牀以足，蔑貞凶。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows one overturning the couch by injuring its legs. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.

lines.ci: 六二，剝牀以辯，蔑貞凶。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one overthrowing the couch by injuring its frame. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.

lines.ci: 六三，剝之無咎。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject among the overthrowers; but there will be no error.

lines.ci: 六四，剝牀以膚，凶。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject having overthrown the couch, and (going to injure) the skin (of him who lies on it). There will be evil.

lines.ci: 六五，貫魚，以宮人寵，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows (its subject leading on the others like) a string of fishes, and (obtaining for them) the favour that lights on the inmates of the palace. There will be advantage in every way.

lines.ci: 上九，碩果不食。君子得輿，小人剝廬。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) a great fruit which has not been eaten. The superior man finds (the people again) as a chariot carrying him. The small men (by their course) overthrow their own dwellings.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Po indicates that (in the state which it symbolises) it will not be advantageous to make a movement in any direction whatever.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams representing) the earth, and (above it) that for a mountain, which adheres to the earth, form Bo. Superiors, in accordance with this, seek to strengthen those below them, to secure the peace and stability of their own position.

hexagrams.name: 复
hexagrams.guaCi: 復，亨。出入無疾，朋來無咎。反覆其道，七日來複。利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷在地中，復。先王以至日閉關，商旅不行，後不省方。

lines.ci: 初九，不遠復，無祗悔，元吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject returning (from an error) of no great extent, which would not proceed to anything requiring repentance. There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 六二，休復，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows the admirable return (of its subject). There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，頻復，厲，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one who has made repeated returns. The position is perilous, but there will be no error.

lines.ci: 六四，中行獨復。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject moving right in the centre (among those represented by the other divided lines), and yet returning alone (to his proper path).

lines.ci: 六五，敦復，無悔。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows the noble return of its subject. There will be no ground for repentance.

lines.ci: 上六，迷復，凶、有災眚。用行師，終有大敗，以其國君凶，至於十年不克徵。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject all astray on the subject of returning. There will be evil. There will be calamities and errors. If with his views he put the hosts in motion, the end will be a great defeat, whose issues will extend to the ruler of the state. Even in ten years he will not be able to repair the disaster.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Fû indicates that there will be free course and progress (in what it denotes). (The subject of it) finds no one to distress him in his exits and entrances; friends come to him, and no error is committed . He will return and repeat his (proper) course. In seven days comes his return. There will be advantage in whatever direction movement is made.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for thunder in the midst of it form Fu. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, on the day. of the (winter) solstice, shut the gates of the passes (from one state to another), so that the travelling merchants could not (then) pursue their journeys, nor the princes go on with the inspection of their states.

hexagrams.name: 无妄
hexagrams.guaCi: 無妄，元享利貞。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天下雷行，物與無妄，先王以茂對時育萬物。

lines.ci: 初九，無妄往，吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from all insincerity. His advance will be accompanied with good fortune.

lines.ci: 六二，不耕穫，不菑畲，則利有攸往。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one who reaps without having ploughed (that he might reap), and gathers the produce of his third year's fields without having cultivated them the first year for that end. To such a one there will be advantage in whatever direction he may move.

lines.ci: 六三，無妄之災，或繫之牛。行人之得，邑人之災。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows calamity happening to one who is free from insincerity;--as in the case of an ox that has been tied up. A passer by finds it (and carries it off), while the people in the neighbourhood have the calamity (of being accused and. apprehended).

lines.ci: 九四，可貞，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case) in which, if its subject can remain firm and correct, there will be no error.

lines.ci: 九五，無妄之疾，勿藥有喜。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows one who is free from insincerity, and yet has fallen ill. Let him not use medicine, and he will have occasion for joy (in his recovery).

lines.ci: 上九：無妄行，有眚，無攸利。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from insincerity, yet sure to fall into error, if he take action. (His action) will not be advantageous in any way.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Wû Wang indicates great progress and success, while there will be advantage in being firm and correct. If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction.
hexagrams.xiangEn: The thunder rolls all under the sky, and to (every)thing there is given (its nature), free from all insincerity. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, (made their regulations) in complete accordance with the seasons, thereby nourishing all things.

hexagrams.name: 大畜
hexagrams.guaCi: 大畜，利貞。不家食，吉。利涉大川。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天在山中，大畜。君子以多識前言往行，以畜其德。

lines.ci: 初九，有厲，利已。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a position of peril. It will be advantageous for him to stop his advance.

lines.ci: 九二，輿說輹。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows a carriage with the strap under it removed.

lines.ci: 九三，良馬逐，利艱貞，吉。日閑輿衛，利有攸往。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject urging his way with good horses. It will be advantageous for him to realise the difficulty (of his course), and to be firm and correct, exercising himself daily in his charioteering and methods of defence;then there will be advantage in whatever direction he may advance.

lines.ci: 六四，童牛之牯，元吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth six, divided, shows the young bull, (and yet) having the piece of wood over his horns. There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 六五，豶豕之牙，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth six, divided, shows the teeth of a castrated hog. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，何天之衢，享。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) in command of the firmament of heaven. There will be progress.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Under the conditions of Tâ Khû it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (If its subject do not seek to) enjoy his revenues in his own family (without taking service at court), there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous for him to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and in the midst of it that (representing) heaven, form Da Xu. The superior man, in accordance with this, stores largely in his memory the words and deeds of former men, to subserve the accumulation of his virtue.

hexagrams.name: 颐
hexagrams.guaCi: 頤，貞吉。觀頤，自求口實。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山下有雷，頤。君子以慎言語，節飲食。

lines.ci: 初九，舍爾靈龜，觀我朵頤，凶。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, (seems to be thus addressed), 'You leave your efficacious tortoise, and look at me till your lower jaw hangs down.' There will be evil.

lines.ci: 六二，顛頤，拂經於丘頤，徵凶。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one looking downwards for nourishment, which is contrary to what is proper; or seeking it from the height (above), advance towards which will lead to evil.

lines.ci: 六三，拂頤，貞凶。十年勿用，無攸利。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows one acting contrary to the method of nourishing. However firm he may be, there will be evil. For ten years let him not take any action, (for) it will not be in any way advantageous.

lines.ci: 六四，顛頤，吉。虎視眈眈，其欲逐逐，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one looking downwards for (the power to) nourish. There will be good fortune. Looking with a tiger's downward unwavering glare, and with his desire that impels him to spring after spring, he will fall into no error.

lines.ci: 六五，拂經，居貞吉，不可涉大川。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one acting contrary to what is regular and proper; but if he abide in firmness, there will be good fortune. He should not, (however, try to) cross the great stream.

lines.ci: 上九，由頤，厲，吉。利涉大川。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom comes the nourishing. His position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Î indicates that with firm correctness there will be good fortune (in what is denoted by it). We must look at what we are seeking to nourish, and by the exercise of our thoughts seek for the proper aliment.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain and under it that for thunder form Yi. The superior man, in accordance with this, (enjoins) watchfulness over our words, and the temperate regulation of our eating and drinking.

hexagrams.name: 大过
hexagrams.guaCi: 大過，棟橈。利有攸往，亨。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤滅木，大過。君子以獨立不懼，遯世無悶。

lines.ci: 初六，藉用白茅，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows one placing mats of the white mâo grass under things set on the ground. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九二，枯楊生稊，老夫得其女妻，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows a decayed willow producing shoots, or an old husband in possession of his young wife. There will be advantage in every way.

lines.ci: 九三，棟橈，凶。《象》曰：棟橈之凶，不可以有輔也。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows a beam that is weak. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 九四，棟隆，吉。有它吝。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows a beam curving upwards. There will be good fortune. If (the subject of it) looks for other (help but that of line one), there will be cause for regret.

lines.ci: 九五，枯楊生華，老婦得其士夫，無咎無譽。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows a decayed willow producing flowers, or an old wife in possession of her young husband. There will be occasion neither for blame nor for praise.

lines.ci: 上六，過涉滅頂，凶，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with extraordinary (boldness) wading through a stream, till the water hides the crown of his head. There will be evil, but no ground for blame.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Tâ Kwo suggests to us a beam that is weak. There will be advantage in moving (under its conditions) in any direction whatever; there will be success.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) trees hidden beneath that for the waters of a marsh forms Da Guo. The superior man, in accordance with this, stands up alone and has no fear, and keeps retired from the world without regret.

hexagrams.name: 坎
hexagrams.guaCi: 坎，習坎，有孚。維心亨，行有尚。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：水洊至，習坎。君子以常德行習教事。

lines.ci: 初六，習坎，入於坎窞，凶。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject in the double defile, and (yet) entering a cavern within it. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 九二，坎有險，求小得。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject in all the peril of the defile. He will, however, get a little (of the deliverance) that he seeks.

lines.ci: 六三，來之坎坎，險且枕，入於坎窞，勿用。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject, whether he comes or goes ( =descends or ascends), confronted by a defile. All is peril to him and unrest. (His endeavours) will lead him into the cavern of the pit. There should be no action (in such a case).

lines.ci: 六四，樽酒簋，貳用缶。納約自牖，終無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (at a feast), with (simply) a bottle of spirits, and a subsidiary basket of rice, while (the cups and bowls) are (only) of earthenware. He introduces his important lessons (as his ruler's) intelligence admits. There will in the end be no error.

lines.ci: 九五，坎不盈，祇既平，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the water of the defile not yet full, (so that it might flow away); but order will (soon) be brought about. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 上六：係用徽纆，寘於叢棘，三歲不得，凶。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject bound with cords of three strands or two strands, and placed in the thicket of thorns. But in three years he does not learn the course for him to pursue. There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Khan, here repeated, shows the possession of sincerity, through which the mind is. penetrating. Action (in accordance with this) will be of high value.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The representation of) water flowing on continuously forms the repeated Kan. The superior man, in accordance with this, maintains constantly the virtue (of his heart) and (the integrity of) his conduct, and practises the business of instruction.

hexagrams.name: 离
hexagrams.guaCi: 離，利貞，亨。畜牝牛，吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：明兩作離，大人以繼明照於四方。

lines.ci: 初九，履錯然，敬之，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows one ready to move with confused steps. But he treads at the same time reverently, and there will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 六二，黃離，元吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject in his place in yellow. There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，日昃之離，不鼓缶而歌，則大耋之嗟，凶。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a position like that of the declining sun. Instead of playing on his instrument of earthenware, and singing to it, he utters the groans of an old man of eighty. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 九四，突如其來如，焚如，死如，棄如。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the manner of its subject's coming. How abrupt it is, as with fire, with death, to be rejected (by all)!

lines.ci: 六五，出涕沱若，戚嗟若，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject as one with tears flowing in torrents, and groaning in sorrow. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，王用出征，有嘉折首，獲匪其醜，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows the king employing its subject in his punitive expeditions. Achieving admirable (merit), he breaks (only) the chiefs (of the rebels). Where his prisoners were not their associates, he does not punish. There will be no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Lî indicates that, (in regard to what it denotes), it will be advantageous to be firm and correct, and that thus there will be free course and success.Let (its subject) also nourish (a docility like that of) the cow, and there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram for) brightness, repeated, forms Li. The great man, in accordance with this, cultivates more and more his brilliant (virtue), and diffuses its brightness over the four quarters (of the land).

hexagrams.name: 咸
hexagrams.guaCi: 咸，亨，利貞，取女吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山上有澤，咸。君子以虛受人。

lines.ci: 初六，咸其拇。
lines.ciEn: The first six, divided, shows one moving his great toes.

lines.ci: 六二，咸其腓，凶。居吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows one moving the calves of his leg. There will be evil. If he abide (quiet in his place), there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，咸其股，執其隨，往咎。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows one moving his thighs, and keeping close hold of those whom he follows. Going forward (in this way) will cause regret.

lines.ci: 九四，貞吉，悔亡。憧憧往來，朋從爾思。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows that firm correctness whi.ch will lead to good fortune, and prevent all occasion for repentance. If its subject be unsettled in his movements, (only) his friends will follow his purpose.

lines.ci: 九五，咸其脢，無悔。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows one moving the flesh along the spine above the heart. There will be no occasion for repentance.

lines.ci: 上六，咸其輔頰舌。
lines.ciEn: The sixth six, divided, shows one moving his jaws and tongue.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Hsien indicates that, (on the fulfilment of the conditions implied in it), there will be free course and success. Its advantageousness will depend on the being firm and correct, (as) in marrying a young lady. There will be good fortune.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for (the waters of) a marsh form Xian. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps his mind free from pre-occupation, and open to receive (the influences of) others.

hexagrams.name: 恒
hexagrams.guaCi: 恆，亨，無咎，利貞。利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷風，恆。君子以立不易方。

lines.ci: 初六，浚恆，貞凶，無攸利。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject deeply (desirous) of long continuance. Even with firm correctness there will be evil; there will be no advantage in any way.

lines.ci: 九二，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows all occasion for repentance disappearing.

lines.ci: 九三，不恆其德，或承之羞，貞吝。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows one who does not continuously maintain his virtue. There are those who will impute this to him as a disgrace. However firm he may be, there will be ground for regret.

lines.ci: 九四，田無禽。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows a field where there is no game.

lines.ci: 六五，恆其德，貞，婦人吉，夫子凶。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject continuously maintaining the virtue indicated by it. In a wife this will be fortunate; in a husband, evil.

lines.ci: 上六，震恆，凶。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject exciting himself to long continuance. There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Hăng indicates successful progress and no error (in what it denotes). But the advantage will come from being firm and correct; and movement in any direction whatever will be advantageous.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for wind form Heng. The superior man, in accordance with this, stands firm, and does not change his method (of operation).

hexagrams.name: 遁
hexagrams.guaCi: 遯，亨。小利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天下有山，遯。君子以遠小人，不惡而嚴。

lines.ci: 初六，遯尾，厲，勿用有攸往。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows a retiring tail. The position is perilous. No movement in any direction should be made.

lines.ci: 六二，執之用黃牛之革，莫之勝說。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject holding (his purpose) fast as if by a (thong made from the) hide of a yellow ox, which cannot be broken.

lines.ci: 九三，係遯，有疾厲，畜臣妾吉。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows one retiring but bound,--to his distress and peril. (If he were to deal with his binders as in) nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for him.

lines.ci: 九四，好遯，君子吉，小人否。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring notwithstanding his likings. In a superior man this will lead to good fortune; a small man cannot attain to this.

lines.ci: 九五，嘉遯，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring in an admirable way. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，肥遯，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring in a noble way. It will be advantageous in every respect.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Thun indicates successful progress (in its circumstances). To a small extent it will (still) be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the sky and below it that for a mountain form Dun. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps small men at a distance, not by showing that he hates them, but by his own. dignified gravity.

hexagrams.name: 大壮
hexagrams.guaCi: 大壯，利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷在天上，大壯。君子以非禮弗履。

lines.ci: 初九，壯於趾，徵凶有孚。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject manifesting his strength in his toes. But advance will lead to evil,--most certainly.

lines.ci: 九二，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows that with firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，小人用壯，君子用罔，貞厲。羝羊觸藩，羸其角。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows, in the case of a small man, one using all his strength; and in the case of a superior man, one whose rule is not to do so. Even with firm correctness the position would be perilous. (The exercise of strength in it might be compared to the case of) a ram butting against a fence, and getting his horns entangled.

lines.ci: 九四，貞吉，悔亡。藩決不羸，壯於大輿之腹。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case in which) firm correctness leads to good fortune, and occasion for repentance disappears. (We see) the fence opened without the horns being entangled. The strength is like that in the wheel-spokes of a large waggon.

lines.ci: 六五，喪羊於易，無悔。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one who loses his ram(-like strength) in the ease of his position. (But) there will be no occasion for repentance.

lines.ci: 上六，羝羊觸藩，不能退，不能遂，無攸利，艱則吉。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows (one who may be compared to) the ram butting against the fence, and unable either to retreat, or to advance as he would fain do. There will not be advantage in any respect; but if he realise the difficulty (of his position), there will be good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Tâ Kwang indicates that (under the conditions which it symbolises) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) heaven and above it that for thunder form Da Zhuang. The superior man, in accordance with this, does not take a step which is not according to propriety.

hexagrams.name: 晋
hexagrams.guaCi: 晉，康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：明出地上。晉。君子以自昭明德。

lines.ci: 初六，晉如，摧如，貞吉。罔孚，裕無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows one wishing to advance, and (at the same time) kept back. Let him be firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. If trust be not reposed in him, let him maintain a large and generous mind, and there will be no error.

lines.ci: 六二，晉如，愁如，貞吉。受茲介福於其王母。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, and yet of being sorrowful. If he be firm and correct, there will be good fortune. He will receive this great blessing from his grandmother.

lines.ci: 六三，眾允，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject trusted by all (around him). All occasion for repentance will disappear.

lines.ci: 九四，晉如鼫鼠，貞厲。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, but like a marmot. However firm and correct he may be, the position is one of peril.

lines.ci: 六五，悔亡，矢得勿恤，往吉，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows how all occasion for repentance disappears (from its subject). (But) let him not concern himself about whether he shall fail or succeed. To advance will be fortunate, and in every way advantageous.

lines.ci: 上九，晉其角，惟用伐邑，厲吉無咎，貞吝。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows one advancing his horns. But he only uses them to punish the (rebellious people of his own) city. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. (Yet) however firm and correct he may be, there will be occasion for regret.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In Žin we see a prince who secures the tranquillity (of the people) presented on that account with numerous horses (by the king), and three times in a day received at interviews.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for the bright (sun) coming forth above it form Jin. The superior man, according to this, gives himself to make more brilliant his bright virtue.

hexagrams.name: 明夷
hexagrams.guaCi: 明夷，利艱貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：明入地中，明夷。君子以蒞眾，用晦而明。

lines.ci: 初九，明夷於飛，垂其翼。君子於行，三日不食。有攸往，主人有言。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, flying, but with drooping wings. When the superior man (is revolving) his going away, he may be for three days without eating. Wherever he goes, the people there may speak (derisively of him).

lines.ci: 六二，明夷於左股，用拯馬壯，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, wounded in the left thigh. He saves himself by the strength of a (swift) horse; and is fortunate.

lines.ci: 九三，明夷於南狩，得其大首，不可疾貞。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, hunting in the south, and taking the great chief (of the darkness). He should not be eager to make (all) correct (at once).

lines.ci: 六四，入於左腹，獲明夷之心，於出門庭。
lines.ciEn: The fourth six, divided, shows its subject (just) entered into the left side of the belly (of the dark land). (But) he is able to carry out the mind appropriate (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, quitting the gate and courtyard (of the lord of darkness).

lines.ci: 六五，箕子之明夷，利貞。
lines.ciEn: The fifth six, divided, shows how the count of K î fulfilled the condition indicated by Ming Î. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.

lines.ci: 上六，不明晦，初登於天，後入於地。
lines.ciEn: The sixth six, divided, shows the case where there is no light, but (only) obscurity. (Its subject) had at first ascended to (the top of) the sky; his future shall be to go into the earth.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Ming Î indicates that (in the circumstances which it denotes) it will be advantageous to realise the difficulty (of the position), and maintain firm correctness.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for the bright (sun) entering within it form Ming Yi. The superior man, in accordance with this, conducts his management of men; - he shows his intelligence by keeping it obscured.

hexagrams.name: 家人
hexagrams.guaCi: 家人，利女貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：風自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恆。

lines.ci: 初九，閑有家，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject establishing restrictive regulations in his household Occasion for repentance will disappear.

lines.ci: 六二，無攸遂，在中饋，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject taking nothing on herself, but in her central place attending to the preparation of the food. Through her firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，家人嗃嗃，悔厲吉。婦子嘻嘻，終吝。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (treating) the members of the household with stern severity. There will be occasion for repentance, there will be peril, (but) there will (also) be good fortune. If the wife and children were to be smirking and chattering, in the end there would be occasion for regret.

lines.ci: 六四，富家大吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject enriching the family. There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 九五，王假有家，勿恤，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the influence of the king extending to his family. There need be no anxiety; there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，有孚威如，終吉。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity and arrayed in majesty. In the end there will be good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: For (the realisation of what is taught in) Kiâ Zăn, (or for the regulation of the family), what is most advantageous is that the wife be firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) fire, and that for wind coming forth from it, form Jia Ren. The superior man, in accordance with this, orders his words according to (the truth of) things, and his conduct so that it is uniformly consistent.

hexagrams.name: 睽
hexagrams.guaCi: 睽，小事吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：上火下澤，睽。君子以同而異。

lines.ci: 初九，悔亡，喪馬，勿逐，自復。見惡人，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. He has lost his horses, but let him not seek for them;--they will return of themselves. Should he meet with bad men, he will not err (in communicating with them).

lines.ci: 九二，遇主於巷，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject happening to meet with his lord in a bye-passage. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六三，見輿曳，其牛掣。其人天且劓，無初有終。
lines.ciEn: In the third SIX, divided, we see one whose carriage is dragged back, while the oxen in it are pushed back, and he is himself subjected to the shaving of his head and the cutting off of his nose. There is no good beginning, but there will be a good end.

lines.ci: 九四，睽孤，遇元夫，交孚，厲，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (But) he meets with the good man (represented by the first line), and they blend their sincere desires together. The position is one of peril, but there will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 六五，悔亡，厥宗噬膚，往何咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. With his relative (and minister he unites closely and readily) as if he were biting through a piece of skin. When he goes forward (with this help), what error can there be?

lines.ci: 上九，睽孤，見豕負塗，載鬼一車。先張之弧，後說之壺，匪寇婚媾。往，遇雨則吉。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (In the subject of the third line, he seems to) see a pig bearing on its back a load of mud, (or fancies) there is a carriage full of ghosts. He first bends his bow against him, and afterwards unbends it, (for he discovers) that he is not an assailant to injure, but a near relative. Going forward, he shall meet with (genial) rain, and there will be good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Khwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) fire above, and that for (the waters of) a marsh below, form Kui. The superior man, in accordance with this, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.

hexagrams.name: 蹇
hexagrams.guaCi: 蹇，利西南，不利東北。利見大人。貞吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山上有水，蹇。君子以反身脩德。

lines.ci: 初六，往蹇，來譽。
lines.ciEn: From the first SIX, divided, we learn that advance (on the part of its subject) will lead to (greater) difficulties, while remaining stationary will afford ground for praise.

lines.ci: 六二，王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows the minister of the king struggling with difficulty on difficulty, and not with a view to his own advantage.

lines.ci: 九三，往蹇，來反。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and returns (to his former associates).

lines.ci: 六四，往蹇，來連。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above).

lines.ci: 九五，大蹇，朋來。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject struggling with the greatest difficulties, while friends are coming to help him.

lines.ci: 上六，往蹇，來碩吉，利見大人。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject going forward, (only to increase) the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will be (productive of) great (merit). There will be good fortune, and it will be advantageous to meet with the great man.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In (the state indicated by) Kien advantage will be found in the south-west, and the contrary in the north-east. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man. (In these circumstances), with firmness and correctness, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and above it that for water, form Jian. The superior man, in accordance with this, turns round (and examines) himself, and cultivates his virtue.

hexagrams.name: 解
hexagrams.guaCi: 解，利西南，無所往，其來複吉。有攸往，夙吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷雨作，解。君子以赦過宥罪。

lines.ci: 初六，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows that its subject will commit no error.

lines.ci: 九二，田獲三狐，得黃矢，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject catch, in hunting, three foxes, and obtain the yellow (= golden) arrows. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，負且乘，致寇至，貞吝。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows a porter with his burden, (yet) riding in a carriage. He will (only) tempt robbers to attack him. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be cause for regret.

lines.ci: 九四，解而拇，朋至斯孚。
lines.ciEn: (To the subject of) the fourth NINE, undivided, (it is said), 'Remove your toes. Friends will (then) come, between you and whom there will be mutual confidence.'

lines.ci: 六五，君子維有解，吉。有孚於小人。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows (its subject), the superior man (= the ruler), executing his function of removing (whatever is injurious to the idea of the hexagram), in which case there will he good fortune, and confidence in him will be shown even by the small men.

lines.ci: 上六，公用射隼於高墉之上，獲之，無不利。
lines.ciEn: In the sixth SIX, divided, we see a feudal prince (with his bow) shooting at a falcon on the top of a high wall, and hitting it. (The effect of his action) will be in every way advantageous.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In (the state indicated by) Kieh advantage will be found in the south-west. If no (further) operations be called for, there will be good fortune in coming back (to the old conditions). If some operations be called for, there will be good fortune in the early conducting of them.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for rain, with these phenomena in a state of manifestation, form Jie. The superior man, in accordance with this, forgives errors, and deals gently with crimes.

hexagrams.name: 损
hexagrams.guaCi: 損，有孚，元吉，無咎。可貞，利有攸往。曷之用？二簋可用享。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山下有澤，損。君子以懲忿窒欲。

lines.ci: 初九，祀事遄往，無咎，酌損之。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject suspending his own affairs, and hurrying away (to help the subject of the fourth line). He will commit no error, but let him consider how far he should contribute of what is his (for the other).

lines.ci: 九二，利貞，徵凶，弗損，益之。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject to maintain a firm correctness, and that action on his part will be evil. He can give increase (to his correlate) without taking from himself.

lines.ci: 六三，三人行，則損一人。一人行，則得其友。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows how of three men walking together, the number is diminished by one; and how one, walking, finds his friend.

lines.ci: 六四，損其疾，使遄有喜，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject diminishing the ailment under which he labours by making (the subject of the first line) hasten (to his help), and make him glad. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六五，或益之十朋之龜，弗克違，元吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows parties adding to (the stores of) its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells, and accepting no refusal. There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，弗損，益之，無咎，貞吉。利有攸往，得臣無家。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject giving increase to others without taking from himself. There will be no error. With firm correctness there will be good fortune. There will be advantage in every movement that shall be made. He will find ministers more than can be counted by their clans.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In (what is denoted by) Sun, if there be sincerity (in him who employs it), there will be great good fortune:--freedom from error; firmness and correctness that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that shall be made. In what shall this (sincerity in the exercise of Sun) be employed? (Even) in sacrifice two baskets of grain, (though there be nothing else), may be presented.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain and beneath it that for the waters of a marsh form Sun. The superior man, in accordance with this, restrains his wrath and represses his desires.

hexagrams.name: 益
hexagrams.guaCi: 益，利有攸往。利涉大川。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：風雷，益。君子以見善則遷，有過則改。

lines.ci: 初九，利用為大作，元吉，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject in his position to make a great movement. If it be greatly fortunate, no blame will be imputed to him.

lines.ci: 六二，或益之十朋之龜，弗克違，永貞吉。王用享於帝，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows parties adding to the stores of its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells whose oracles cannot be opposed. Let him persevere in being firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. Let the king, (having the virtues thus distinguished), employ them in presenting his offerings to God, and there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，益之用凶事，無咎。有孚中行，告公用圭。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows increase given to its subject by means of what is evil, so that he shall (be led to good), and be without blame. Let him be sincere and pursue the path of the Mean, (so shall he secure the recognition of the ruler, like) an officer who announces himself to his prince by the symbol of his rank.

lines.ci: 六四，中行，告公從，利用為依遷國。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject pursuing the due course. His advice to his prince is followed. He can with advantage be relied on in such a movement as that of removing the capital.

lines.ci: 九五，有孚惠心，勿問，元吉。有孚惠我德。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with sincere heart seeking to benefit (all below). There need be no question about it; the result will be great good fortune. (All below) will with sincere heart acknowledge his goodness.

lines.ci: 上九，莫益之，或擊之，立心勿恆，凶。
lines.ciEn: In the sixth NINE, undivided, we see one to whose increase none will contribute, while many will seek to assail him. He observes no regular rule in the ordering of his heart. There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Yî indicates that (in the state which it denotes) there will be advantage in every movement which shall be undertaken, that it will be advantageous (even) to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) wind and that for thunder form Yi. The superior man, in accordance with this, when he sees what is good, moves towards it; and when he sees his errors, he turns from them.

hexagrams.name: 夬
hexagrams.guaCi: 夬，揚於王庭。孚號有厲，告自邑。不利即戎，利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤上於天，夬。君子以施祿及下，居德則忌。

lines.ci: 初九，壯於前趾，往不勝為咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject in (the pride of) strength advancing with his toes. He goes forward, but will not succeed. There will be ground for blame.

lines.ci: 九二，惕號，莫夜有戎，勿恤。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject full of apprehension and appealing (for sympathy and help). Late at night hostile measures may be (taken against him), but he need not be anxious about them.

lines.ci: 九三，壯於頄，有凶。君子夬夬，獨行遇雨。若濡有慍，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (about to advance) with strong (and determined) looks. There will be evil. (But) the superior man, bent on cutting off (the criminal), will walk alone and encounter the rain, (till he be hated by his proper associates) as if he were contaminated (by the others). (In the end) there will be no blame against him.

lines.ci: 九四，臀無膚，其行次且。牽羊悔亡，聞言不信。
