lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped, and who walks slowly and with difficulty. (If he could act) like. a sheep led (after its companions), occasion for repentance would disappear. But though he hear these words, he will not believe them.

lines.ci: 九五，陸夬夬，中行無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows (the small men like) a bed of purslain, which ought to be uprooted with the utmost determination. (The subject of the line having such determination), his action, in harmony with his central position, will lead to no error or blame.

lines.ci: 上六，無號，終有凶。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject without any (helpers) on whom to call. His end will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kwâi requires (in him who would fulfil its meaning) the exhibition (of the culprit's guilt) in the royal court, and a sincere and earnest appeal (for sympathy and support), with a consciousness of the peril (involved in cutting off the criminal). He should (also) make announcement in his own city, and show that it will not be well to have recourse at once to arms. (In this way) there will be advantage in whatever he shall go forward to.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) heaven and that for the waters of a marsh mounting above it form Guai. The superior man, in accordance with this, bestows emolument on those below him, and dislikes allowing his gifts to accumulate (undispensed).

hexagrams.name: 姤
hexagrams.guaCi: 姤，女壯，勿用取女。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：天下有風，姤。後以施命誥四方。

lines.ci: 初六，繫於金柅，貞吉。有攸往，見凶。羸豕孚蹢躅。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows how its subject should be kept (like a carriage) tied and fastened to a metal drag, in which case with firm correctness there will be good fortune. (But) if he move in any direction, evil will appear. He will be (like) a lean pig, which is sure to keep jumping about.

lines.ci: 九二，包有魚，無咎，不利賓。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject with a wallet of fish. There will be no error. But it will not be well to let (the subject of the first line) go forward to the guests.

lines.ci: 九三，臀無膚，其行次且，厲，無大咎。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped so that he walks with difficulty. The position is perilous, but there will be no great error.

lines.ci: 九四，包無魚，起凶。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with his wallet, but no fish in it. This will give rise to evil.

lines.ci: 九五，以杞苞瓜，含章，有隕自天。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, (shows its subject as) a medlar tree overspreading the gourd (beneath it). If he keep his brilliant qualities concealed, (a good issue) will descend (as) from Heaven.

lines.ci: 上九，姤其角，吝，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject receiving others on his horns. There will be occasion for regret, but there will be no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kâu shows a female who is bold and strong. It will not be good to marry (such) a female.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) wind and that for the sky above it form Gou. The sovereign, in accordance with this, delivers his charges, and promulgates his announcements throughout the four quarters (of the kingdom).

hexagrams.name: 萃
hexagrams.guaCi: 萃，亨，王假有廟。利見大人，亨，利貞。用大牲吉，利有攸往。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤上於地，萃。君子以除戎器，戒不虞。

lines.ci: 初六，有孚不終，乃亂乃萃。若號，一握為笑，勿恤，往無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject with a sincere desire (for union), but unable to carry it out, so that disorder is brought into the sphere of his union. If he cry out (for help to his proper correlate), all at once (his tears) will give place to smiles. He need not mind (the temporary difficulty); as he goes forward, there will be no error.

lines.ci: 六二，引吉，無咎。孚乃利用禴。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject led forward (by his correlate). There will be good fortune, and freedom from error. There is entire sincerity, and in that case (even the small offerings of) the vernal sacrifice are acceptable.

lines.ci: 六三，萃如嗟如，無攸利，往無咎，小吝。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject striving after union and seeming to sigh, yet nowhere finding any advantage. If he go forward, he will not err, though there may be some small cause for regret.

lines.ci: 九四，大吉無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject in such a state that, if he be greatly fortunate, he will receive no blame.

lines.ci: 九五，萃有位，無咎，匪孚。元永貞，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the union (of all) under its subject in the place of dignity. There will be no error. If any do not have confidence in him, let him see to it that (his virtue) be great, long-continued, and firmly correct, and all occasion for repentance will disappear.

lines.ci: 上六，齎咨涕洟，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject sighing and weeping; but there will be no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In (the state denoted by) Žhui, the king will repair to his ancestral temple. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man; and then there will be progress and success, though the advantage must come through firm correctness. The use of great victims will conduce to good fortune; and in whatever direction movement is made, it will be advantageous.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing the) earth and that for the waters of a marsh raised above it form Cui. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his weapons of war put in good repair, to be prepared against unforeseen contingencies.。

hexagrams.name: 升
hexagrams.guaCi: 升，元亨。用見大人，勿恤。南征吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：地中生木，升。君子以順德，積小以成高大。

lines.ci: 初六，允升，大吉。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards with the welcome (of those above him). There will be great good fortune.

lines.ci: 九二，孚乃利用禴，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject with that sincerity which will make even the (small) offerings of the vernal sacrifice acceptable. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九三，升虛邑。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject ascending upwards (as into) an empty city.

lines.ci: 六四，王用享於岐山，吉，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject employed by the king to present his offerings on mount Kh î. There will be good fortune; there will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 六五，貞吉，升階。
lines.ciEn: The fifth six, divided, shows its subject firmly correct, and therefore enjoying good fortune. He ascends the stairs (with all due ceremony).

lines.ci: 上六，冥升，利於不息之貞。
lines.ciEn: The sixth six, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards blindly. Advantage will be found in a ceaseless maintenance of firm correctness.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Shăng indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. Seeking by (the qualities implied in it) to meet with the great man, its subject need have no anxiety. Advance to the south will be fortunate.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) wood and that for the earth with the wood growing in the midst of it form Sheng. The superior man, in accordance with this, pays careful attention to his virtue, and accumulates the small developments of it till it is high and great.

hexagrams.name: 困
hexagrams.guaCi: 困，亨，貞大人吉，無咎。有言不信。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤無水，困。君子以致命遂志。

lines.ci: 初六，臀困於株木。入於幽谷，三歲不覿。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject with bare buttocks straitened under the stump of a tree. He enters a dark valley, and for three years has no prospect (of deliverance).

lines.ci: 九二，困於酒食，朱紱方來，利用亨祀，徵凶。無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject straitened amidst his wine and viands. There come to him anon the red knee-covers (of the ruler). It will be well for him (to maintain his sincerity as) in sacrificing. Active operations (on his part) will lead to evil, but he will be free from blame.

lines.ci: 六三，困於石，據於蒺藜，入於其宮，不見其妻，凶。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened before a (frowning) rock. He lays hold of thorns. He enters his palace, and does not see his wife. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 九四，來徐徐，困於金車，吝，有終。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided shows its subject proceeding very slowly (to help the subject of the first line), who is straitened by the carriage adorned with metal in front of him. There will be occasion for regret, but the end will be good.

lines.ci: 九五，劓刖，困於赤紱，乃徐有說，利用祭祀。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with his nose and feet cut off. He is straitened by (his ministers in their) scarlet aprons. He is leisurely in his movements, however, and is satisfied. It will be well for him to be (as sincere) as in sacrificing (to spiritual beings).

lines.ci: 上六，困於葛藟，於臲卼，曰動悔有悔，徵吉。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened, as if bound with creepers; or n a high and dangerous position, and saying (to himself), 'If I move, I shall repent it.' If he do repent of former errors, there will be good fortune in his going forward.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: In (the condition denoted by) Khwăn there may (yet be) progress and success. For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune. He will fall into no error. If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a marsh, and (below it that for a defile, which has drained the other dry so that there is) no water in it, form Kun. The superior man, in accordance with this, will sacrifice his life in order to carry out his purpose.

hexagrams.name: 井
hexagrams.guaCi: 井，改邑不改井，無喪無得，往來井井。汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶，凶。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：木上有水，井。君子以勞民勸相。

lines.ci: 初六，井泥不食，舊井無禽。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows a well so muddy that men will not drink of it; or an old well to which neither birds (nor other creatures) resort.

lines.ci: 九二，井谷射鮒，瓮敝漏。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows a well from which by a hole the water escapes and flows away to the shrimps (and such small creatures among the grass), or one the water of which leaks away from a broken basket.

lines.ci: 九三，井渫不食，為我心惻。可用汲，王明，並受其福。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows a well, which has been cleared out, but is not used. Our hearts are sorry for this, for the water might be drawn out and used. If the king were (only) intelligent, both he and we might receive the benefit of it.

lines.ci: 六四，井甃，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows a well, the lining of which is well laid. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九五，井冽，寒泉食。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows a clear, limpid well, (the waters from) whose cold spring are (freely) drunk.

lines.ci: 上六，井收勿幕，有孚元吉。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows (the water from) the well brought to the top, which is not allowed to be covered. This suggests the idea of sincerity. There will be great good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: (Looking at) Žing, (we think of) how (the site of) a town may be changed, while (the fashion of) its wells undergoes no change. (The water of a well) never disappears and never receives (any great) increase, and those who come and those who go can draw and enjoy the benefit. If (the drawing) have nearly been accomplished, but, before the rope has quite reached the water, the bucket is broken, this is evil.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for water form Jing. The superior man, in accordance with this, comforts the people, and. stimulates them to mutual helpfulness.

hexagrams.name: 革
hexagrams.guaCi: 革，已日乃孚，元亨利貞，悔亡。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤中有火，革。君子以治曆明時。

lines.ci: 初九，鞏用黃牛之革。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as if he were) bound with the skin of a yellow ox.

lines.ci: 六二，已日乃革之，徵吉，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject making his changes after some time has passed. Action taken will be fortunate. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九三，徵凶，貞厲。革言三就，有孚。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows that action taken by its subject will be evil. Though he be firm and correct, his position is perilous. If the change (he contemplates) have been three times fully discussed, he will be believed in.

lines.ci: 九四，悔亡，有孚，改命吉。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows occasion for repentance disappearing (from its subject). Let him be believed in; and though he change (existing) ordinances, there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九五，大人虎變，未占有孚。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the great man (producing his changes) as the tiger (does when he) changes (his stripes). Before he divines (and proceeds to action), faith has been reposed in him.

lines.ci: 上六，君子豹變，小人革面，徵凶。居貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the superior man producing his changes as the leopard (does when he) changes (his spots), while small men change their faces (and show their obedience). To go forward (now) would lead to evil, but there will be good fortune in abiding firm and correct.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: (What takes place as indicated by) Ko is believed in only after it has been accomplished. There will be great progress and success. Advantage will come from being firm and correct. (In that case) occasion for repentance will disappear.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and that for fire in the midst of them form Ge. The superior man, in accordance with this, regulates his (astronomical) calculations, and makes clear the seasons and times.

hexagrams.name: 鼎
hexagrams.guaCi: 鼎，元吉，亨。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：木上有火，鼎。君子以正位凝命。

lines.ci: 初六，鼎顛趾，利出否。得妾以其子，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows the caldron overthrown and its feet turned up. (But) there will be advantage in its getting rid of what was bad in it. (Or it shows us) the concubine (whose position is improved) by means of her son. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九二，鼎有實，我仇有疾，不我能即，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with the things (to be cooked) in it. (If its subject can say), 'My enemy dislikes me, but he cannot approach me,' there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，鼎耳革，其行塞，雉膏不食。方雨，虧悔，終吉。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with (the places of) its ears changed. The progress (of its subject) is (thus) stopped. The fat flesh of the pheasant (which is in the caldron) will not be eaten. But the (genial) rain will come, and the grounds for repentance will disappear. There will be good fortune in the end.

lines.ci: 九四，鼎折足，覆公餗，其形渥，凶。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with its feet broken; and its contents, designed for the ruler's use, overturned and spilt. Its Subject will be made to blush for shame. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 六五，鼎黃耳，金鉉，利貞。
lines.ciEn: The fifth six, divided, shows the caldron with yellow ears and rings of metal in them. There will be advantage through being firm and correct.

lines.ci: 上九，鼎玉鉉，大吉，無不利。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with rings of jade. There will be great good fortune, and all action taken will be in every way advantageous.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Ting gives the intimation of great progress and success.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for fire form Ding. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps his every position correct, and maintains secure the appointment (of Heaven).

hexagrams.name: 震
hexagrams.guaCi: 震，亨。震來虩虩，笑言啞啞，震驚百裡，不喪匕鬯。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：洊雷震，君子以恐懼修省。

lines.ci: 初九，震來虩虩，後笑言啞啞，吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, looking out and around with apprehension, and afterwards smiling and talking cheerfully. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六二，震來厲，億喪貝，躋於九陵，勿逐，七日得。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, in a position of peril. He judges it better to let go the articles (in his possession), and to ascend a very lofty height. There is no occasion for him to pursue after (the things he has let go); in seven days he will find them.

lines.ci: 六三，震蘇蘇，震行無眚。
lines.ciEn: The third six, divided, shows its subject distraught amid the startling movements going on. If those movements excite him to (right) action, there will be no mistake.

lines.ci: 九四，震遂泥。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject, amid the startling movements, supinely sinking (deeper) in the mud.

lines.ci: 六五，震，往來厲，億，無喪有事。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject going and coming amidst the startling movements (of the time), and always in peril; but perhaps he will not incur loss, and find business (which he can accomplish).

lines.ci: 上六，震索索，視矍矍，徵凶。震不於其躬，於其鄰，無咎。婚媾有言。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject, amidst the startling movements (of the time), in breathless dismay and looking round him with trembling apprehension. If he take action, there will be evil. If, while the startling movements have not reached his own person and his neighbourhood, (he were to take precautions), there would be no error, though his relatives might (still) speak against him.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kăn gives the intimation of ease and development. When (the time of) movement (which it indicates) comes, (the subject of the hexagram) will be found looking out with apprehension, and yet smiling and talking cheerfully. When the movement (like a crash of thunder) terrifies all within a hundred lî, he will be (like the sincere worshipper) who is not (startled into) letting go his ladle and (cup of) sacrificial spirits.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) thunder, being repeated, forms Zhen. The superior man, in accordance with this, is fearful and apprehensive, cultivates (his virtue), and examines (his faults).

hexagrams.name: 艮
hexagrams.guaCi: 艮其背，不獲其身，行其庭，不見其人，無咎。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：兼山艮。君子以思不出其位。

lines.ci: 初六，艮其趾，無咎，利永貞。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his toes at rest. There will be no error; but it will be advantageous for him to be persistently firm and correct.

lines.ci: 六二，艮其腓，不拯其隨，其心不快。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping the calves of his legs at rest. He cannot help (the subject of the line above) whom he follows, and is dissatisfied in his mind.

lines.ci: 九三，艮其限，裂其夤，厲閽心。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject keeping his loins at rest, and separating the ribs (from the body below). The situation is perilous, and the heart glows with suppressed excitement.

lines.ci: 六四，艮其身，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his trunk at rest. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六五，艮其輔，言有孚，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his jawbones at rest, so that his words are (all) orderly. Occasion for repentance will disappear.

lines.ci: 上九：敦艮，吉。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject devotedly maintaining his restfulness. There will be good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: When one's resting is like that of the back, and he loses all consciousness of self; when he walks in his courtyard, and does not see any (of the persons) in it,--there will be no error.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (Two trigrams representing) a mountain, one over the other, form Gen. The superior man, in accordance with this, does not go in his thoughts beyond the (duties of the) position in which he is.

hexagrams.name: 渐
hexagrams.guaCi: 漸，女歸吉，利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山上有木，漸。君子居賢德善俗。

lines.ci: 初六，鴻漸於乾，小子厲，有言，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows the wild geese gradually approaching the shore. A young officer (in similar circumstances) will be in a position of danger, and be spoken against; but there will be no error.

lines.ci: 六二，鴻漸於磐，飲食衎衎，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows the geese gradually approaching the large rocks, where they eat and drink joyfully and at ease. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，鴻漸於陸，夫徵不復，婦孕不育，凶。利用禦寇。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows them gradually advanced to the dry plains. (It suggests also the idea of) a husband who goes on an expedition from which he does not return, and of a wife who is pregnant, but will not nourish her child. There will be evil. (The case symbolised) might be advantageous in resisting plunderers.

lines.ci: 六四，鴻漸於木，或得其桷，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the trees. They may light on the flat branches. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九五，鴻漸於陵，婦三歲不孕，終莫之勝，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the high mound. (It suggests the idea of) a wife who for three years does not become pregnant; but in the end the natural issue cannot be prevented. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，鴻漸於陸，其羽可用為儀，吉。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the large heights (beyond). Their feathers can be used as ornaments. There will be good fortune.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kien suggests to us the marriage of a young lady, and the good fortune (attending it). There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for a tree form Jian. The superior man, in accordance with this, attains to and maintains his extraordinary virtue, and makes the manners of the people good.

hexagrams.name: 归妹
hexagrams.guaCi: 歸妹，徵凶，無攸利。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤上有雷，歸妹。君子以永終知敝。

lines.ci: 初九，歸妹以娣，跛能履，徵吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows the younger sister married off in a position ancillary to the real wife. (It suggests the idea of) a person lame on one leg who yet manages to tramp along. Going forward will be fortunate.

lines.ci: 九二，眇而視，利幽人之貞。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows her blind of one eye, and yet able to see. There will be advantage in her maintaining the firm correctness of a solitary widow.

lines.ci: 六三，歸妹以須，反歸以娣。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows the younger sister who was to be married off in a mean position. She returns and accepts an ancillary position.

lines.ci: 九四，歸妹愆期，遲歸有時。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the younger sister who is to be married off protracting the time. She may be late in being married, but the time will come.

lines.ci: 六五，帝乙歸妹，其君之袂，不如其娣之袂良。月幾望，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, reminds us of the marrying of the younger sister of (king) Tî-yî, when the sleeves of her the princess were not equal to those of the (still) younger sister who accompanied her in an inferior capacity. (The case suggests the thought of) the moon almost full. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，女承筐無實，士刲羊無血，無攸利。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the young lady bearing the basket, but without anything in it, and the gentleman slaughtering the sheep, but without blood flowing from it. There will be no advantage in any way.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kwei Mei indicates that (under the conditions which it denotes) action will be evil, and in no wise advantageous.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and over it that for thunder form Gui Mei. The superior man, in accordance with this, having regard to the far-distant end, knows the mischief (that may be done at the beginning).

hexagrams.name: 丰
hexagrams.guaCi: 豐，亨，王假之，勿憂，宜日中。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：雷電皆至，豐。君子以折獄致刑。

lines.ci: 初九，遇其配主，雖旬無咎，往有尚。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject meeting with his mate. Though they are both of the same character, there will be no error. Advance will call forth approval.

lines.ci: 六二，豐其蔀，日中見鬥，往得疑疾。有孚發若，吉。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject surrounded by screens so large and thick that at midday he can see from them the constellation of the Bushel. If he go (and try to enlighten his ruler who is thus emblemed), he will make himself to be viewed with suspicion and dislike. Let him cherish his feeling of sincere devotion that he may thereby move (his ruler's mind), and there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九三，豐其沛，日中見沬，折其右肱，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject with an (additional) screen of a large and thick banner, through which at midday he can see (the small) Mei star. (In the darkness) he breaks his right arm; but there will be no error.

lines.ci: 九四，豐其蔀，日中見鬥，遇其夷主，吉。
lines.ciEn: T he fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a tent so large and thick that at midday he can see from it the constellation of the Bushel. But he meets with the subject of the (first) line, undivided like himself. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六五，來章，有慶譽，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject bringing around him the men of brilliant ability. There will be occasion for congratulation and praise. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上六，豐其屋，蔀其家。闚其戶，闃其無人。三歲不覿，凶。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with his house made large, but only serving as a screen to his household. When he looks at his door, it is still, and there is nobody about it. For three years no one is to be seen. There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Făng intimates progress and development. When a king has reached the point (which the name denotes) there is no occasion to be anxious (through fear of a change). Let him be as the sun at noon.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigrams representing) thunder and lightning combine to form Feng. The superior man, in accordance with this, decides cases of litigation, and apportions punishments with exactness.

hexagrams.name: 旅
hexagrams.guaCi: 旅，小亨，旅貞吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山上有火，旅。君子以明慎用刑，而不留獄。

lines.ci: 初六，旅瑣瑣，斯其所取災。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows the stranger mean and meanly occupied. It is thus that he brings on himself (further) calamity.

lines.ci: 六二，旅即次，懷其資，得僮僕貞。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows the stranger, occupying his lodging-house, carrying with him his means of livelihood, and provided with good and trusty servants.

lines.ci: 九三，旅焚其次，喪其僮僕，貞厲。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows the stranger, burning his lodging-house, and having lost his servants. However firm and correct he (try to) be, he will be in peril.

lines.ci: 九四，旅於處，得其資斧，我心不快。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the traveller in a resting-place, having (also) the means of livelihood and the axe, (but still saying), 'I am not at ease in my mind.'

lines.ci: 六五，射雉，一矢亡，終以譽命。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject shooting a pheasant. He will lose his arrow, but in the end he will obtain praise and a (high) charge.

lines.ci: 上九，鳥焚其巢，旅人先笑後號咷，喪牛於易，凶。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a bird burning its nest. The stranger, (thus represented), first laughs and then cries out. He has lost his ox(-like docility) too readily and easily. There will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Lü intimates that (in the condition which it denotes) there may be some little attainment and progress. If the stranger or traveller be firm and correct as he ought to be, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for fire form Lu. The superior man, in accordance with this, exerts his wisdom and caution in the use of punishments and not allowing litigations to continue.

hexagrams.name: 巽
hexagrams.guaCi: 巽，小亨，利有攸往，利見大人。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：隨風，巽。君子以申命行事。

lines.ci: 初六，進退，利武人之貞。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (now) advancing, (now) receding. It would be advantageous for him to have the firm correctness of a brave soldier.

lines.ci: 九二，巽在牀下，用史巫紛若，吉，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows the representative of Sun beneath a couch, and employing diviners and exorcists in a way bordering on confusion. There will be good fortune and no error.

lines.ci: 九三，頻巽，吝。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject penetrating (only) by violent and repeated efforts. There will be occasion for regret.

lines.ci: 六四，悔亡，田獲三品。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows all occasion for repentance (in its subject) passed away. He takes game for its threefold use in his hunting.

lines.ci: 九五，貞吉，悔亡，無不利，無初有終。先庚三日，後庚三日，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows that with firm correctness there will be good fortune (to its subject). All occasion for repentance will disappear, and all his movements will be advantageous. There may have been no (good) beginning, but there will be a (good) end. Three days before making any changes, (let him give notice of them); and three days after, (let him reconsider them). There will (thus) be good fortune.

lines.ci: 《上九，巽在牀下，喪其資斧，貞凶。
lines.ciEn: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the representative of penetration beneath a couch, and having lost the axe with which he executed his decisions. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Sun intimates that (under the conditions which it denotes) there will be some little attainment and progress. There will be advantage in movement onward in whatever direction. It will be advantageous (also) to see the great man.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (Two trigrams representing) wind, following each other, form Xun. The superior man, in accordance with this, reiterates his orders, and secures the practice of his affairs.

hexagrams.name: 兑
hexagrams.guaCi: 兌，亨，利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：麗澤，兌，君子以朋友講習。

lines.ci: 初九，和兌，吉。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows the pleasure of (inward) harmony. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九二，孚兌，吉，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows the pleasure arising from (inward) sincerity. There will be good fortune. Occasion for repentance will disappear.

lines.ci: 六三，來兌，凶。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject bringing round himself whatever can give pleasure. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 九四，商兌未寧，介疾有喜。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject deliberating about what to seek his pleasure in, and not at rest. He borders on what would be injurious, but there will be cause for joy.

lines.ci: 九五，孚於剝，有厲。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject trusting in one who would injure him. The situation is perilous.

lines.ci: 上六，引兌。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows the pleasure of its subject in leading and attracting others.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Tui intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (Two symbols representing) the waters of a marsh, one over the other, form Dui. The superior man, in accordance with this, (encourages) the conversation of friends and (the stimulus of) their (common) practice.

hexagrams.name: 涣
hexagrams.guaCi: 渙，亨。王假有廟，利涉大川，利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：風行水上，渙。先王以享於帝，立廟。

lines.ci: 初六，用拯馬壯，吉。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject engaged in rescuing (from the impending evil) and having (the assistance of) a strong horse. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 九二，渙奔其機，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject, amid the dispersion, hurrying to his contrivance (for security). All occasion for repentance will disappear.

lines.ci: 六三，渙其躬，無悔。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject discarding any regard to his own person. There will be no occasion for repentance.

lines.ci: 六四，渙其群，元吉。渙有丘，匪夷所思。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject scattering the (different) parties (in the state); which leads to great good fortune. From the dispersion (he collects again good men standing out, a crowd) like a mound, which is what ordinary men would not have thought of.

lines.ci: 九五，渙汗其大號。渙王居，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject amidst the dispersion issuing his great announcements as the perspiration (flows from his body). He scatters abroad (also) the accumulations in the royal granaries. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 上九，渙其血，去逖出，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject disposing of (what may be called) its bloody wounds, and going and separating himself from its anxious fears. There will be no error.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Hwân intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. The king goes to his ancestral temple; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) water and that for wind moving above the water form Huan. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, presented offerings to God and established the ancestral temple.

hexagrams.name: 节
hexagrams.guaCi: 節，亨，苦節不可貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤上有水，節。君子以制數度，議德行。

lines.ci: 初九，不出戶庭，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject not quitting the courtyard outside his door. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九二，不出門庭，凶。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject not quitting the courtyard inside his gate. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 六三，不節若，則嗟若，無咎。
lines.ciEn: . The third SIX, divided, shows its subject with no appearance of observing the (proper) regulations, in which case we shall see him lamenting. But there will be no one to blame (but himself).

lines.ci: 六四，安節，亨。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject quietly and naturally (attentive to all) regulations. There will be progress and success.

lines.ci: 九五，甘節，吉。往有尚。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject sweetly and acceptably enacting his regulations. There will be good fortune. The onward progress with them will afford ground for admiration.

lines.ci: 上六，苦節，貞凶，悔亡。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject enacting regulations severe and difficult. Even with firmness and correctness there will be evil. But though there will be cause for repentance, it will (by and by) disappear.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kieh intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) if the regulations (which it prescribes) be severe and difficult, they cannot be permanent.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a lake, and above it that for water, form Jie. The superior man, in accordance with this, constructs his (methods of) numbering and measurement, and discusses (points of) virtue and conduct.

hexagrams.name: 中孚
hexagrams.guaCi: 中孚豚魚吉。利涉大川。利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：澤上有風，中孚。君子以議獄緩死。

lines.ci: 初九，虞吉，有它不燕。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject resting (in himself). There will be good fortune. If he sought to any other, he would not find rest.

lines.ci: 九二：鳴鶴在陰，其子和之，我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject (like) the crane crying out in her hidden retirement, and her young ones responding to her. (It is as if it were said), 'I have a cup of good spirits,' (and the response were), 'I will partake of it with you.'

lines.ci: 六三，得敵，或鼓或罷，或泣或歌。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject having met with his mate. Now he beats his drum, and now he leaves off. Now he weeps, and now he sings.

lines.ci: 六四，月幾望，馬匹亡，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (like) the moon nearly full, and (like) a horse (in a chariot) whose fellow disappears. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九五：有孚攣如，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject perfectly sincere, and linking (others) to him in closest union. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 上九：翰音登於天，貞凶。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject in chanticleer (trying to) mount to heaven. Even with firm correctness there will be evil.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kung Fû (moves even) pigs and fish, and leads to good fortune. There will be advantage in crossing the great stream. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and that for wind above it form Zhong Fu. The superior man, in accordance with this, deliberates about cases of litigation and delays (the infliction of) death.

hexagrams.name: 小过
hexagrams.guaCi: 小過，亨，利貞。可小事，不可大事。飛鳥遺之音，不宜上，宜下，大吉。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：山上有雷，小過。君子以行過乎恭，喪過乎哀，用過乎儉。

lines.ci: 初六，飛鳥以凶。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, suggests (the idea of) a bird flying, (and ascending) till the issue is evil.

lines.ci: 六二，過其祖，遇其妣，不及其君，遇其臣，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject passing by his grandfather, and meeting with his grandmother; not attempting anything against his ruler, but meeting him as his minister. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 九三，弗過防之，從或戕之，凶。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject taking no extraordinary precautions against danger; and some in consequence finding opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil.

lines.ci: 九四，無咎，弗過遇之，往厲必戒，勿用永貞。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject falling into no error, but meeting (the exigency of his situation), without exceeding (in his natural. course). If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious. There is no occasion to be using firmness perpetually.

lines.ci: 六五，密雲不雨，自我西郊。公弋取彼在穴。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, (suggests the idea) of dense clouds, but no rain, coming from our borders in the west. It also (shows) the prince shooting his arrow, and taking the bird in a cave.

lines.ci: 上六，弗遇過之，飛鳥離之，凶，是謂災眚。
lines.ciEn: The sixth SIX, divided, shows. its subject not meeting (the exigency of his situation), and exceeding (his proper course). (It suggests the idea of) a bird flying far aloft. There will be evil. The case is what is called one of calamity and self-produced injury.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Hsiâo Kwo indicates that (in the circumstances which it implies) there will be progress and attainment.But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (What the name denotes) may be done in small affairs, but not in great affairs. (It is like) the notes that come down from a bird on the wing;--to descend is better than to ascend. There will (in this way) be great good fortune.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) a hill and that for thunder above it form Xiao Guo. The superior man, in accordance with this, in his conduct exceeds in humility, in mourning exceeds in sorrow, and in his expenditure exceeds in economy.

hexagrams.name: 既济
hexagrams.guaCi: 既濟，亨小，利貞。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：水在火上，既濟。君子以思患而豫防之。

lines.ci: 初九，曳其輪，濡其尾，無咎。
lines.ciEn: The first NINE, undivided, (shows its subject as a driver) who drags back his wheel, (or as a fox) which has wet his tail. There will be no error.

lines.ci: 六二，婦喪其茀，勿逐，七日得。
lines.ciEn: The second SIX, divided, (shows its subject as) a wife who has lost her (carriage-)screen. There is no occasion to go in pursuit of it. In seven days she will find it.

lines.ci: 九三，高宗伐鬼方，三年克之，小人勿用。
lines.ciEn: The third NINE, undivided, (suggests the case of) Kâo Žung, who attacked the Demon region, but was three years in subduing it. Small men should not be employed (in such enterprises).

lines.ci: 六四，繻有衣袽，終日戒。
lines.ciEn: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject with rags provided against any leak (in his boat), and on his guard all day long.

lines.ci: 九五，東鄰殺牛，不如西鄰之禴祭，實受其福。
lines.ciEn: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) the neighbour in the east who slaughters an ox (for his sacrifice); but this is not equal to the (small) spring sacrifice of the neighbour in the west, whose sincerity receives the blessing.

lines.ci: 上六，濡其首，厲。
lines.ciEn: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with (even) his head immersed. The position is perilous.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Kî Žî intimates progress and success in small matters. There will be advantage in being firm and correct. There has been good fortune in the beginning; there may be disorder in the end.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) fire and that for water above it form Ji Ji. The superior man, in accordance with this, thinks of evil (that may come), and beforehand guards against it.

hexagrams.name: 未济
hexagrams.guaCi: 未濟，亨。小狐汔濟，濡其尾，無攸利。
hexagrams.xiang: 《象》曰：火在水上，未濟。君子以慎，辯物居方。

lines.ci: 初六，濡其尾，吝。
lines.ciEn: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (like a fox) whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.

lines.ci: 九二，曳其輪，貞吉。
lines.ciEn: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject dragging back his (carriage-) wheel. With firmness and correctness there will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 六三，未濟，徵凶，利涉大川。
lines.ciEn: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject, with (the state of things) not yet remedied, advancing on; which will lead to evil. But there will be advantage in (trying to) cross the great stream.

lines.ci: 九四，貞吉，悔亡。震用伐鬼方，三年有賞於大邦。
lines.ciEn: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, so that all occasion for repentance disappears. Let him stir himself up, as if he were invading the Demon region, where for three years rewards will come to him (and his troops) from the great kingdom.

lines.ci: 六五，貞吉，無悔。君子之光，有孚，吉。
lines.ciEn: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, and having no occasion for repentance. (We see in him) the brightness of a superior man, and the possession of sincerity. There will be good fortune.

lines.ci: 上九，有孚於飲酒，無咎。濡其首，有孚失是。
lines.ciEn: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject full of confidence and therefore feasting (quietly). There will be no error. (If he) cherish this confidence, till he (is like the fox who) gets his head immersed, it will fail of what is right.

hexagrams.guaCiEn: Wei Žî intimates progress and success (in the circumstances which it implies). (We see) a young fox that has nearly crossed (the stream), when its tail gets immersed. There will be no advantage in any way.
hexagrams.xiangEn: (The trigram representing) water and that for fire above it form Wei Ji. The superior man, in accordance with this, carefully discriminates among (the qualities of) things, and the (different) positions they (naturally) occupy.

100000.poem: 周师伐纣，克于牧野。甲子平旦，天下悦喜。
100000.poemEn: Zhou’s army smites Zhou of Yin — victory at Muye; at jiazi’s dawn — all under Heaven rejoices.
100000.comment: 震为周、为伐，坤为师、为恶，故为纣。坤为野、为养，故曰牧野。牧者，养也。乾初爻正值甲子，震为晨，故曰甲子平旦。坤为天下，震为悦喜。

100001.poem: 噂噂所言，莫如我垣。欢乐坚固，可以长安。
100001.poemEn: Rumors hum and buzz — none as secure as my wall; joy firm and stable — we may dwell long in peace.
100001.comment: 《毛传》："噂，对语也"。震为言，正覆震相对，故曰噂噂。艮为垣，正覆艮相对而艮为止，故曰莫如。如，往也。震为欢喜，艮为坚固、为安。○垣，宋元本讹恒，依汲古。

100010.poem: 悬貆素飡，食非其任。失舆剥庐，休坐徙居，室家何忧。
100010.poemEn: Hanging badger and eating plain fare — not our proper charge; carriage lost and hut stripped — we rest then shift our home — what has the household to fear?
100010.comment: 艮貆，艮阳在上故曰悬貆。震为口、为白，故曰素飡。《诗魏风》："胡瞻尔庭有悬貆兮，彼君子兮，不素餐兮"，飡，即餐也。震为食、为舆，坤丧故失舆。艮为庐，坎破故剥庐。艮为坐、为居，震行故徙居。艮为室家，坎为忧，震乐故无忧。○貆，宋元本、汲古本作狟，依湖北局本，与诗合。飡，元本作餐，依宋本、汲古。按：《说文》狟，犬行也。《广韵》狟与貆通。然三本皆作狟，是焦诗本作狟。

100011.poem: 襦烧裤燔，羸剥饥寒，病虐冻挛。
100011.poemEn: Jacket burned and trousers scorched — thin and stripped in hunger and cold; sick with ague — frozen and cramped.
100011.comment: 震为襦，巽为裤，艮为火，故曰烧燔。p s坤为羸，艮手为剥，坤为饥寒、为病虐、为冻。挛，系也。《说文》凡拘牵连系者皆曰挛。○第三句病虐汲古作病症，依宋元。挛，宋本作孪，依汲古。孪，《说文》双生也，宋本非。

100100.poem: 猿堕高木，不踒手足。握珠怀玉，还归我室。
100100.poemEn: An ape falls from a high tree — hands and feet unhurt; pearls in hand and jade to the breast — I return to my house.
100100.comment: 艮为猿，震为木、为足，艮为手。踒，折也。艮在震上，故猿堕高木。震为珠玉、为归，艮为握、为室。○踒，汲古作跛，依宋元本。

100101.poem: 逐禽出门，并失玉丸。往来井井，破甑缺益。
100101.poemEn: Chasing birds out the door — I lose my jade pellets; going and coming in order — cracked jars break all the more.
100101.comment: 震为逐、为出，艮为禽、为门。坎为失、为弹丸，震为玉，故曰玉丸。兑为井，初四伏正反兑，故曰往来井井。震为甑、为益，坎为破、为缺。○破甑，元本作破瓮，汲古作甑破，依宋本。

100110.poem: 五心六意，歧道多怪。非君本志，生我恨悔。
100110.poemEn: Five minds and six intents — at the forks are many marvels; not the ruler’s true heart — it breeds my regret.
100110.comment: 巽卦数五，互大坎，为心意数六，震为道路、为君。

100111.poem: 踦牛伤暑，不能成亩。草莱不鬬，年岁无有。
100111.poemEn: A limping ox hurt by heat — cannot finish the field; weeds not fought — the year bears no yield.
100111.comment: 京房以《无妄》为大旱之卦。艮为火故曰暑，为牛，巽下断，故曰踦牛。坤为亩，二阴故不成亩。巽为草莱，乾为年岁，巽陨落故无年。

101000.poem: 尧饮舜舞，禹拜上酒。礼乐所丰，可以安处，保我淑女。
101000.poemEn: Yao drinks and Shun dances — Yu bows and offers wine; rites and music abundant — we dwell at ease, guarding our good lady.
101000.comment: 震为帝，故曰尧舜禹。震为饮、为舞，坎为酒，坤为礼，震为乐。

101001.poem: 孟春醴酒，使君寿考。南山多福，宜行贾市。
101001.poemEn: Early spring sweet wine — to make the lord long-lived; South Mountain rich in blessing — fit to go forth to trade.
101001.comment: 稻梁雌雉，所至利喜。震为春、为长，故曰孟春。坎为酒，震为君，艮为寿考、为南山。伏巽为贾市、为稻梁。离为雌。○孟春，汲古作春孟，依宋元本。稻梁，汲古作秋梁，依宋元本。

101010.poem: 驱羊南行，与祸相逢。狼惊吾马，虎盗我子，悲恨自咎。
101010.poemEn: Driving sheep south — we meet with disaster; a wolf startles my horse, a tiger steals my child — sorrow and self-reproach.
101010.comment: 此用《复》象。震为羊、为驱、为南、为行，坤为祸、为狼虎，震为马、为惊、为子，伏巽为盗。坤为悲恨。

101011.poem: 大一置酒，乐正起舞。万福攸同，可以安处，绥我齯齿。
101011.poemEn: On the great day we set out wine — the music-master rises to dance; ten thousand blessings together — we dwell at ease and comfort our elders.
101011.comment: 大一，即北辰。《史记天官书》："中宫天极星，其一明者大一，常居也"，注：天神最尊贵者。离为星，故曰大一。坎为酒，伏震为乐、为舞、为万福，兑为齿，卦有两半兑形故曰齯齿。《尔雅》："黄发齯齿"，注：齿隳更生细者。古单作儿。按：今诗正作儿齿。○大一，宋本、汲古俱作大乙，依元本。齯，汲古作见，依宋元本。

101100.poem: 九雁列阵，雌独不群。为罾所牵，死于庖人。
101100.poemEn: Nine wild geese in ranks — one hen not in the flock; caught by the net’s pull — she dies by the butcher’s hand.
101100.comment: 震为雁，数九，故曰九雁。震为阵，巽为雌，在后，故曰不群。离为罾，兑折故死。震为人。

101101.poem: 桀跖并处，民困愁苦。行旅迟迟，留连齐鲁。
101101.poemEn: Jie and Zhi dwell together — the people pressed and in sorrow; travelers move slowly — lingering in Qi and Lu.
101101.comment: 离为恶人，故曰桀。巽为盗，故曰跖。伏坎为众、为民、为愁苦，伏震为行旅，艮止故曰迟、曰留连。巽为齐，兑为鲁。○首句元本作跖桀并处，汲古作跖并桀处，今依宋本。

101110.poem: 天厌禹德，命兴汤国。祓社衅鼓，以除民疾。
101110.poemEn: Heaven tires of Yu’s virtue — commands Tang’s state to rise; purge the altar and blood the drum — to drive out the people’s ills.
101110.comment: 通《蒙》。艮为天，震为王，故曰禹。坤为国、为水，故曰汤国。坤为社，震为鼓，坤为民，坎为疾，震乐故除疾。○第三句元本作祅社衅鼓，依宋本、汲古。

101111.poem: 凶忧灾殃，日益章明。祸不可救，三却夷伤。
101111.poemEn: Ill worries and disaster — daily more manifest; harm cannot be remedied — thrice we withdraw, the border folk are hurt.
101111.comment: 详《噬嗑》之《剥》。○首句依《噬嗑》之《剥》校改，各本皆作"恶灾殆盈"，惟三却彼取象于退，此以巽隙取象，离数三，故曰三却。

110000.poem: 尚利壤义，月出平地。国乱天常，咎徵灭亡。
110000.poemEn: Coveting profit and casting aside right — the moon rises over flatland; the state offends Heaven’s constant — omens of blame end in ruin.
110000.comment: 伏巽为利，坤为义，兑毁故曰坏义。兑为月，坤为平地、为国、为灭亡。月出平地，用象神妙。○首句宋元本作"尚刑怀义"，依汲古。

110001.poem: 把珠入口，蓄为玉宝。得吾所有，欣然嘉喜。
110001.poemEn: A pearl to the mouth — stored as jade treasure; what was mine I obtain — gladly, with joy.
110001.comment: 震为珠玉，兑为口，坤为吾，震为喜，艮手为把。

110010.poem: 簪短带长，幽思苦穷。瘠蠡小，以病之癃。
110010.poemEn: Short pin and long belt — hidden thoughts bitter and poor; thin and meager — sickly and crippled.
110010.comment: 艮为簪，兑折，故簪短。伏巽为带、为长，坎为幽思、为瘠。，音陶，病也。○短，各本皆作跌，蠡作貌，依《恒》之《咸》校改。蠡，音祼。《左传桓六年》："谓其不疾瘯蠡也"，注：疥病。小，宋本作小瘦，汲古作小疲，依元本。又苦穷各本皆作穷苦。病之隆，各本皆作疾病降，均依《恒》之《咸》校。

110011.poem: 三人俱行，各别采桑。蕴其筐筥，留我嘉旅。
110011.poemEn: Three travel together — each goes to gather mulberry; baskets heaped high — they lodge my honored guest.
110011.comment: 得归无咎，四月来处。震为人、为行，数三，故曰三人俱行。艮手为采，巽为桑，震为筐筥、为行旅、为归，兑为月，数四，故曰四月。艮为处。○旅，汲古作侣，非，依宋元本。

110100.poem: 东行破车，远反失家。天命讫终，无所祷凶。
110100.poemEn: Going east the cart breaks — far returning, we lose our home; Heaven’s allotment has run out — no prayer can avert misfortune.
110100.comment: 震为东、为行、为车，兑毁故破车。震为反，艮为家，艮伏故失家。伏巽为命，艮为天、为终，兑口为祷。○远反失家，言反目远处而无家也，与上句对文，汲古作还反室家，宋本作远反室家，皆非，今依元本。

110101.poem: 白马騧骝，生乳不休。富我商人，得利饶优。
110101.poemEn: White horse and piebald roan — foaling without cease; they enrich my merchant — profits abundant.
110101.comment: 坎为马，兑西方，色白故曰白马。伏艮为乳，马乳可为酒。《汉书礼乐志》："以马乳为酒"，撞挏乃成。卦有两半艮，故曰生乳不休。三四句疑亦用半象。○騧，汲古作騂，从宋元本。

110110.poem: 赋敛重数，政为民贼。杼柚空虚，去其家室。
110110.poemEn: Levies heavy and often — rule becomes a thief to the people; looms stand empty — they leave their homes.
110110.comment: 详《否》之《丰》。第四句汲古作"家去其室"，依宋元本。

110111.poem: 十五许室，柔顺有德。霜降既嫁，文以为合。先王日至，不利出域。
110111.poemEn: At fifteen betrothal allowed — gentle and virtuous; after frost she is wed — writ seals the match; on the day of former kings — unfit to go beyond the bounds.
110111.comment: 兑数十，巽卦数五，故曰十五。伏坎为室，震为言，故曰许室，言以女字人也。坤为柔顺，坎为霜，震为嫁，坤为文，坎为合，诗文定厥祥是也。震为王，《谦》三至上复为日至。丁晏云：《周礼媒氏》疏王肃引《韩诗传》："古者霜降，逆女冰泮杀止"，《荀子大略篇》说同。又引《家语》云"霜降而妇功成，嫁娶者行焉；冰泮而农业起，昏礼杀于此"，兹云"霜降既嫁"，是焦氏说与《荀子》、《韩诗》说合，由是证《诗》"迨冰未泮"，言及冰未泮而归妻，若已泮则杀止。《郑笺》谓正月中冰未泮，至二月可以昏者，非也。○既，汲古作归，文作夫，均依宋元本。《复》象云"先王以至日闭关，商旅不行，后不省方"，故云不利出域。

111000.poem: 任力劣薄，远托邦国。辅车不强，为痈所伤。
111000.poemEn: Weak in burden and force — leaning on distant states; jaw and cheek not strong — harmed by swelling sores.
111000.comment: 震健故曰任力。坤为邦国、为车，坤柔故曰不强。伏艮为节、为痈，兑为伤。○托，汲古作托，强作僵，依宋元本。

111001.poem: 南邦大国，鬼魅满室。欢声相逐，为我行贼。
111001.poemEn: In the great southern state — ghosts fill the rooms; cries of joy chase each other — yet they act as thieves against me.
111001.comment: 乾为南，艮为邦国，伏巽为鬼魅。艮为室，震为乐、为声、为逐，伏巽为贼。《杂卦》巽伏也，伏故为鬼、为盗贼。○国，汲古作域，依宋元本。

111010.poem: 东风解冻，河川流通。西门子产，升擢有功。
111010.poemEn: East wind loosens the freeze — rivers run free; Ximen Zichan is raised and promoted — his merit acknowledged.
111010.comment: 坎为冻，离为东，故曰东风解冻。坎为河川，位西，乾为门，故曰西门。魏西门豹、郑子产皆循吏，乾为贵，故曰升擢有功。

111011.poem: 车驰人趋，卷甲相仇。齐鲁寇战，败于犬邱。
111011.poemEn: Carts race and men hasten — armor rolled tight, they feud; Qi and Lu raid and battle — defeated at Dog Mound.
111011.comment: 详《坤》之《兑》。

111100.poem: 三羝上山，俱至阴安。遂到南阳，见其芝香。两崖相望，未同枕床。
111100.poemEn: Three rams climb the mountain — all reach the shade and rest; then we come to Nanyang — we find the scent of lingzhi; two cliffs face each other — not yet one pillow and bed.
111100.comment: 兑为羊，震数三，故曰三羝。艮为山，艮反故曰阴，言至山北也。乾为南、为阳，兑为见，伏巽为芝、为吞，伏艮为崖，兑卦数二，故曰两崖，大壮上形似之。艮为枕、为床，艮伏故曰未同枕床。○见，汲古作完，同作有，均依宋元本。

111101.poem: 冠危戴患，身惊不安。与福驰逐，凶来入门。
111101.poemEn: Crown tilts and trouble worn — the body startles, ill at ease; racing with blessing — misfortune comes through the door.
111101.comment: 通《比》。坎为危患，艮为冠戴、为身，坎陷故不安。艮为门，坤为凶。○戴，汲古作载，依宋元本。

111110.poem: 水沫沉浮，沮湿不居，为心疾忧。通《剥》。
111110.poemEn: Foam on water, sinking and floating — sodden and damp, unfit to dwell; worry like a sickness of the heart.
111110.comment: 坤为水，一阳在上故曰水沫沉浮、曰沮湿。坤为心、为疾忧。

111111.poem: 任武负力，东征不伏。蹈泥履涂，雄师败覆。
111111.poemEn: Trusting in force and bearing strength — eastward the campaign gains no submission; treading mud and mire — the mighty host is routed.
111111.comment: 此用遇卦"复"象。震为武、为东征、为蹈，履坤为水、为泥涂、为师，坤丧故败覆。○第三句汲古作"陷履泥涂"，宋本作"陷泥履涂"，兹依元本。

000000.poem: 义不胜情，以欲自营。觊利危躬，折角摧颈。
000000.poemEn: Duty cannot overrule desire — craving governs the self; coveting profit endangers the body — horns snapped, neck crushed.
000000.comment: 坤为义、为情欲、为躬，坤死故危躬。艮为角、为颈，《复》下震为覆艮，艮覆故曰折角摧颈。此亦全用遇卦象。○觊，元本作为，依宋木、汲古。躬，宋元本作宠，从汲古。

010001.poem: 鷂鴟娶婦，深目窈身。折腰不媚，与伯相背。
010001.poemEn: The kite and the owl take a wife — deep eyes, slender form; she will not bow or flatter — she turns her back on the elder.
010001.comment: 艮为鷂鴟。震为娶，坤为妇，互大离故曰深目。坤为身、为黑，故曰窈身。坎为腰、为折，震为武、为健，故曰不媚。震为伯，艮为背。○鶹●鶹亦●属，宋元作鹞，依汲古。

010111.poem: 三足俱行，倾危善僵。六指不便，慁累弟兄。树柱阂车，失其正当。
010111.poemEn: Three legs go together — easy to topple and fall; six fingers are clumsy — they burden the brothers; a post set up blocks the cart — the proper way is lost.
010111.comment: 详《贲》之《咸》。 ○慁累，汲古作累慁，宋元作恩累，兹依《贲》之《咸》校。

010000.poem: 京庾积仓，黍稷以兴。极行疾至，以餍饱食。
010000.poemEn: Capital granaries piled — millet and rice abound; push on and swiftly arrive — to eat our fill.
010000.comment: 坤为仓庾、为积，震为黍稷、为行、为亟，为疾、为食，坎为饱。○宋元本极上多己字，饱下无食字，非，依汲古。惟汲古行作其，亦非。《诗小雅甫田》篇："曾孙之庾，如坻如京；乃求千斯仓，黍稷稻梁。"极当为亟。

000010.poem: 南山之蹊，真人所在。德配唐虞，天命为子。保佑歆享，身受大庆。
000010.poemEn: On a South Mountain path — the true man dwells; virtue matched with Tang and Yu — Heaven makes him its son; blessed with offerings — great fortune on his person.
000010.comment: 详《贲》之《解》。

000111.poem: 千岁旧室，将有困急。荷粮负囊，出门直北。
000111.poemEn: An old house of a thousand years — meets straits and crisis; grain on the shoulder, a sack on the back — out the door straight north.
000111.comment: 坤为千岁，乾为旧，艮为室，巽为陨落，故曰困急。艮为荷、为负，巽为粮，坤为囊、为门、为北，故曰出门直北。

001000.poem: 虎狼并处，不可以仕。忠谋辅政，祸必及己。退隐深山，身乃不殆。
001000.poemEn: Where tigers and wolves dwell together — unfit to serve; loyal counsel to aid rule — disaster reaches oneself; retire to deep mountains — the body is spared from peril.
001000.comment: 艮为处，狼正覆艮故曰并处。艮为仕，坎险故不可仕。坎为忠、为谋，坤为祸、为己，艮为山，坎为隐，坤为身、为殆，震乐故不殆。○仕、辅政，汲古作事、作辅改，皆非，今依宋元本。殆音以，言与宵小并仕，虽忠必获祸，退隐则免也。

000100.poem: 卵与石鬬，糜碎无处。挈瓶之使，不为忧惧。
000100.poemEn: An egg fights a stone — crushed to paste, nowhere to cling; the pitcher-bearer on duty — he does not fret.
000100.comment: 震为卵，艮为石，震艮相反故曰鬬。坤为浆、为糜，震为瓶，艮手为挈，坎为忧惧。《左传》："虽有挈瓶之知"，注：汲者，喻小知。按：古汲用瓶。

011001.poem: 雨雪载涂，东行破车，旅人无家。
011001.poemEn: Rain and snow mire the road — going east the cart breaks; the traveler has no home.
011001.comment: 震为大涂、为东、为车，互大坎为雨雪，兑折故曰破车。震为商旅、为人，艮为家，在外故曰无家。○宋元本多"利益咨嗟"四字，依汲古。家与涂、车韵。

000011.poem: 东行破车，步入危家。衡门穿射，无以为主。卖袍续食，糟糠不饱。
000011.poemEn: Going east the cart breaks — on foot I enter a perilous house; the crossbar door pierced with arrows — no master within; I sell my robe for food — chaff and dregs leave me unfed.
000011.comment: 此用《复》象。震为东、为车，坤丧故曰破车。震为步、为射、为主、为袍、为糟糠，坤为门，坤虚故无以为主、故不饱。○危，汲古作范，从宋元本。

000001.poem: 持刃操肉，对酒不食。夫亡从军，少子入狱，抱膝独宿。
000001.poemEn: Knife in hand and meat held — yet before wine he does not eat; the husband off to war, the youngest son in jail — hugging knees, she sleeps alone.
000001.comment: 艮手为持、为操、为刃，坤为军，艮为夫，在上，故曰夫亡从军。亡，往也。艮为少子，坤为宿。酒肉象均不详。狱象膝象，疑皆指艮。

011110.poem: 尧舜禹汤，四圣敦仁。允施德音，艮安无穷。旅人相望，未同朝乡。
011110.poemEn: Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang — four sages firm in benevolence; their fair virtue applied — repose without end; travelers look toward each other — not yet one court or land.
011110.comment: 乾为帝王、为圣、为仁，巽数四，故曰四圣。乾为德，兑为口，故曰德音。伏坤为民，艮为安、为望，震为商旅、为向，正反震相对。故曰旅人相望，曰未同朝乡。乡，向也。○乡，汲古、宋本皆讹卿，依元本。下二句与上四句意不属，疑为衍文。

010010.poem: 桎梏拘获，身入牢狱。髠刑受法，终不得释。耳闭道塞，求事不得。
010010.poemEn: Shackled and seized — the body enters prison; shorn by punishment and under the law — never released; ears shut, road blocked — nothing sought is obtained.
010010.comment: 坎为桎梏、为牢狱，伏巽为髠，坎陷故不得释。坎为耳、为闭塞，艮为道路、为求。

001110.poem: 求鸡获雉，买鳖失鱼。出人钧敌，租得无馀。齐姜宋子，婚姻孔喜。
001110.poemEn: Seek a chicken — catch a pheasant; buy a turtle — miss the fish; matched with others in contest — rents leave nothing over; yet Lady Jiang of Qi and the son of Song — the marriage is a great joy.
001110.comment: 艮为求，巽为鸡、为鱼，伏坤为文、为雉，艮为鳖。鸡、雉、鱼、鳖相等，故曰钧敌。巽为利、为齐姜。艮为宋，少男少女相遇故曰婚姻。兑为悦，故曰孔喜。○敌，汲古作货，依宋元本。馀，宋元作饶，依汲古。雉，宋元本作雏。

011100.poem: 雨师驾驷，风伯吹云。秦楚争强，施不得行。
011100.poemEn: The Rain Lord drives a four-in-hand — the Wind Earl blows the clouds; Qin and Chu contend for might — policies cannot be carried out.
011100.comment: 互兑为雨，伏坤为师，震为马，故曰雨师驾驷。巽为风，震为伯，伏坤为云，兑口故曰吹云。兑为秦，震为楚、为争，乾健故曰争强。独断云：雨师，毕星；风伯，箕星也。

001111.poem: 仲冬无秋，鸟鹊饥忧。困于米食，数惊鸇雕。
001111.poemEn: Midwinter with no autumn — birds and magpies hunger and fret; pinched for grain — often startled by hawks and eagles.
001111.comment: 通《临》。复居子，故曰仲冬。兑为秋，坤虚故无秋，言仲冬之时，百物凋落也。艮为鸟鹊，坤为饥、为忧困，震为米，兑为食，艮为鸇雕。○无，汲古讹兼。鸟鹊饥忧，汲古作鸟散饮忧，依宋元本。

000101.poem: 飞之日南，还归辽东。雌友相从，和鸣雍雍，解我胸舂。
000101.poemEn: Flying to the sun’s south — then back to Liaodong; the female mate follows, cooing in accord — it eases my pounding heart.
000101.comment: 离为日、为南、为飞，艮东北，故曰辽东。坎雄离雌，坎为和，艮为胸，艮手为春。胸舂者，言胸臆上下不定，如舂米于胸中也。○之，宋元本作至。胸舂，宋本作逈舂，元本作逈春，均依汲古。

001010.poem: 宛马疾步，盲师坐御。目不见路，中止不到。
001010.poemEn: Curving horses hurry — a blind master sits to drive; seeing not the road — we stop midway and do not arrive.
001010.comment: 宛，踠之省。《后汉书班固传》："马踠馀足"，注：踠，屈也。又《说文》宛：屈草自覆也，是宛亦有屈意。宛马疾步者，言马足既屈而使之速行也。互坎为马，坎为屈，故曰踠马。坎为众，为师，艮离目不全，故曰盲师。艮为坐，御本立，为今以盲师而坐御，故不见路而不到也。艮为路、为止。

010100.poem: 春桃萌生，万物华荣。邦君所居，国乐无忧。
010100.poemEn: Spring peach puts forth — the myriad things flower; where the lord resides — the state is joyful and free of care.
010100.comment: 震为桃、为春、为萌、为生、为华荣、为君、为乐。

011111.poem: 行如乐纣，虽祷不佑。命绝衰周，文君乏祀。
011111.poemEn: Conduct like wanton Zhou of Yin — though you pray, you are not helped; the mandate cut off in declining Zhou — the cultured lord lacks offerings.
011111.comment: 通《复》。坤为恶，故曰桀纣。震为行、为言，故曰祷。震为周、为君，巽为命，坤丧故命绝。坤为文，故曰文君，谓文王也。○佑，宋元本作祥，君作王，均依汲古。

000110.poem: 蜱蜉戴盆，不能上山。脚摧跛蹶，损伤其颜。
000110.poemEn: A tick bears a basin — it cannot climb the mountain; feet shattered, lame and stumbling — the face is marred.
000110.comment: 巽为虫，故曰蜱蜉，艮形似覆盆，故曰戴盆。艮为山，震为足，震覆故曰脚摧、曰跛蹶。兑为损，艮为颜。○蜱蜉，汲古作蜉蝣，颜作头，均依宋本。摧损，宋元本作推顿，均依汲古，元本注云：蚍蜉有翼者曰蜱蜉。

011000.poem: 长子入狱，妇馈母哭。霜降愈甚，向晦伏法。
011000.poemEn: The eldest son jailed — the wife brings food and the mother weeps; frost descends and grows harsher — toward dusk he meets his sentence.
011000.comment: 震为长子，互大坎为狱，巽为妇，坤为母，兑口为哭。坤为霜、为晦，坤死故曰伏法。○愈，汲古作旬，依宋元，疑旬字音讹为甚字。《周礼小司寇》："至于旬，乃弊之"，而宋本作愈，疑原文为霜降逾旬。

010110.poem: 求犬得兔，请新遇故。虽不当路，逾吾旧舍。
010110.poemEn: Seek a dog and get a hare — invite the new and meet the old; though off the road — we pass by our former house.
010110.comment: 通《贲》。艮为犬、为求，震为兔，离为新，坎为故，艮为路、为舍。

011010.poem: 鸟鸣葭端，一呼三颠。动摇东西，危而不安。灵祝祷祉，疾病无患。
011010.poemEn: Birds cry on the reed-tip — one call and thrice it sways; rocking east and west — perilous and ill at ease; with prayers and blessings — sickness brings no harm.
011010.comment: 对《噬嗑》。震为葭、为鸣呼，艮为鸟，坎数一，震数三，离为东，坎为西，坎险故危。震为言，故曰祝祷。坎为疾病，震喜故无患。全用对象，祇颠字用本卦《巽》。○动摇，宋元本作摇动，依汲古。祝，汲古作符，依宋元本。

011101.poem: 阴雾作匿，不见白日。邪径迷道，使君乱惑。
011101.poemEn: Yin mists hide — the white sun unseen; crooked paths confuse the way — the lord falls into turmoil and delusion.
011101.comment: 通《屯》。坤为雾、为阴，坎为匿，故不见。离日，震为白，故曰白日。艮为径、为道，坤为迷、为乱，震为君。○迷道，汲古作迷通，依宋元本。

001001.poem: 三骊负衡，南取芝香。秋兰芬馥，盈满箧筐，利我少姜。
001001.poemEn: Three black horses under the yoke — south we seek lingzhi’s scent; autumn orchids rich with fragrance — baskets brim full — a boon to my young Jiang.
001001.comment: 互震为马，数三，艮为负、为衡，震为南，伏巽为芝、为香、为兰、为芬馥，伏兑为秋，震为筐，巽为利、为姜。○第四句宋元本作盛满匣匮，汲古作盈满匣匮，依局本。

001011.poem: 春生夏乳，羽毛成就。举不失宜，君臣相好。盗走奔北，终无有悔。
001011.poemEn: Born in spring, suckled in summer — feathers complete; every act meets its season — lord and ministers accord; thieves flee north — in the end no regret.
001011.comment: 离为夏，艮为乳，伏震为春、为生、为羽毛、为君，艮为臣，坎为盗、为北，艮为终。○夏，汲古作孚，依宋元本。有悔，宋本作有晦，汲古作所悔，依元本。

001101.poem: 二人辇车，徙去其家。井沸釜鸣，不可以居。
001101.poemEn: Two men push a handcart — moving away from home; the well boils, the pot cries — unfit to dwell.
001101.comment: 详《剥》之《讼》。 ○徙，汲古讹从。下有艮火故井沸。

011011.poem: 闭塞复通，与善相逢。甘棠之人，解我忧凶。
011011.poemEn: Blocked then open again — I meet with the good; the man of the sweet pear-tree — dispels my worry and harm.
011011.comment: 通《震》。互坎为闭塞，震为通、为棠、为人，坎为忧，震通故解。《诗召南甘棠》篇、鲁韩诗说皆谓召公听讼棠下，兹曰解我忧凶是齐说，谓召公平反冤狱于其下也。

010011.poem: 怒非其愿，贪妬腐鼠。而呼鹊鸱，自令失饵，致被殃患。
010011.poemEn: Anger not for desire — greedy jealousy for a rotten mouse; calling magpie and owl — you lose your bait yourself and bring on disaster.
010011.comment: 震为怒，坎为妬，艮为鼠，巽腐，故曰腐鼠。震为呼，艮为鹊鸱，坎为失、为殃患，震为饵。○贪妬，宋本作贪垢，元本作含垢，兹依汲古。致被殃患，汲古作倒被灾患，兹依宋元本。《庄子》："鸱得腐鼠，鵷雏过之，仰而视之曰：吓"。林用其意。

001100.poem: 逐鸠南飞，与喜相随。并获鹿子，多得利归，虽忧不危。
001100.poemEn: Chasing the dove south in flight — joy comes with it; a fawn is taken as well — much profit brought home; though worried, no danger.
001100.comment: 震为逐，艮为鸠，震为南、为飞、为喜、为子、为鹿、为归、为利。

010101.poem: 东邻西国，福喜同乐。出得隋珠，留获和玉，俱利有息。
010101.poemEn: Eastern neighbor and western state — blessing and joy together; going out we gain a Sui pearl, staying we get He jade — both bring profit and increase.
010101.comment: 离为东邻，坎为西国。《既济九五》爻词正如此也，徒以先天象失传，致解者皆误。复震为福喜、为乐、为珠玉、为出，坤闭故曰留。○有息，宋元作有喜，失韵，依汲古。

100000.poem: 夏台羑里，汤文卮处。鬼侯饮食，岐人悦喜。
100000.poemEn: At Xia Terrace and Youli — where Tang and Wen once dwelt; the Ghost Marquis offers food and drink — the people of Qi rejoice.
100000.comment: 此用遇卦《颐》象，义详前《无妄》林。《史记》："西伯、九侯为纣三公，纣烹九侯"，徐广曰，九一作鬼。○首二句依《无妄》校。羑里，各本皆作幽户，汤文作文君。

100001.poem: 家给人足，颂声并作。四夷宾服，乾戈卷阁。
100001.poemEn: Households supplied and people sufficient — songs of praise arise; the four quarters bow as guests — spears and shields are rolled away.
100001.comment: 艮为家，震为人，坤多故给足。震为声。坤阴，故为夷狄，震卦数四，故曰四夷。震为宾，艮为乾戈，艮止故卷阁。

100010.poem: 三雁俱行，避暑就凉。适与矰遇，为缴所伤。
100010.poemEn: Three wild geese fly together — avoiding heat they seek cool; they meet a whistle-arrow — and are struck by the line.
100010.comment: 震为雁，数三，故曰三雁。坎为寒，离伏，故曰避暑就凉。伏巽为矰缴，兑为伤。○矰，元本作缯，依宋本、汲古。行，汲古作飞，依宋元本。

100011.poem: 悬貆素餐，食非其任。失舆剥庐，休坐徙居。
100011.poemEn: Hanging badger and plain fare — not our appointed food; carriage lost and hut stripped — we rest and move our dwelling.
100011.comment: 详《乾》之《震》。○貆，宋元本作狟，徙作从，兹依汲古。

100100.poem: 从商进游，饱食无忧。囹圄之困，中子见囚。
100100.poemEn: Traveling with merchants — we eat our fill, without worry; yet prison’s distress — the middle son is seized.
100100.comment: 震为商、为游、为食，坎中满故饱食。坎为忧，震乐故无。坎为囹圄、为中男，艮止故见囚。○饱食，汲古作食饱，依宋元本。

100101.poem: 随阳转行，不失其常。君安于乡，国无咎殃。
100101.poemEn: Turning with the sun — not losing the norm; the lord at ease in his land — the state free of blame or harm.
100101.comment: 离为日，震为随、为行、为转运，而离上震下，故曰随阳转行。震为君，艮为乡、为国，艮止，故君安而国无殃咎也。

100110.poem: 生不逢时，困且多忧。无有冬夏，心常悲愁。
100110.poemEn: Born out of time — pinched and full of cares; neither winter nor summer — the heart ever sorrowing.
100110.comment: 震为生，艮为时，兑向晦，故生不逢时。艮为困，巽为忧，正反巽，故多忧。震春兑秋，故曰无有冬夏，言无时不悲愁也。

100111.poem: 栋桡榱坏，廊屋大败。宫阙空廓，如冬枯树。
100111.poemEn: Beams warp and rafters break — colonnades collapse; palaces empty and vast — like winter’s withered trees.
100111.comment: 震为榱栋，巽陨落故桡坏。艮为廊屋、为宫阙，巽陨故大败，震虚故空廓。乾为冬，震为树，巽为枯。○空廓，宋元本作空廊，兹依汲古。

101000.poem: 五岳四渎，润洽为德。行不失理，民赖恩福。
101000.poemEn: Five Peaks and Four Streams — their moistening is virtue; act without losing measure — the people rely on grace.
101000.comment: 震为山，坎为五，故曰五岳。震卦数四，坤坎皆为水，故曰四渎、曰润洽。《淮南子》："河润百里"。坤为理、为民。○润，元本作，依宋本、汲古。

101001.poem: 群虎入邑，求索肉食。大人御守，君不失国。
101001.poemEn: A band of tigers enters the town — seeking meat to devour; the great man defends and guards — the lord does not lose his state.
101001.comment: 艮为虎、为邑，正覆艮，故曰群虎。艮为求，坎为肉，故求索肉食。震为大人、为君，艮为守、为国，能守故不失也。

101010.poem: 黄离白日，照我四国。元首昭明，民赖恩福。
101010.poemEn: Bright yellow sun — shining on my four quarters; the head made manifest — the people lean on grace.
101010.comment: 《离九二》：曰"黄离"。离为日、为照。艮为国。震卦数四。故曰四国。艮为首，坤为民，颐本大离，林词全取《颐》象。○恩，从宋元本，汲古作为。

101011.poem: 载车乘马，南逢君子。与我嘉福，虽忧无咎。
101011.poemEn: Cart loaded and horse in traces — south we meet a gentleman; he brings me fair blessing — though worried, no blame.
101011.comment: 此用《颐》象。震为车、为马、为载、为乘、为南，艮为君子，故曰南逢君子。震为嘉福，坤为忧。○福，宋元本作喜，依汲古。

101100.poem: 张目关口，舌直距齿。然诺不行，政乱无绪。
101100.poemEn: Eyes wide, mouth barred — tongue tight against the teeth; promises not kept — governance snarled in disorder.
101100.comment: 离为目，震为张，兑口伏艮，故曰关口。兑为舌、为齿，二至五正反兑相背故曰距。距，抗也。相背，故然诺不行。巽为绪，二至五正反巽，故乱而无绪。此皆用覆象，自覆象失传，《困》"有言不信"等词皆失解。○关，汲古作开，依宋元本。

101101.poem: 一指食肉，口无所得。染其鼎鼐，舌馋于腹。
101101.poemEn: One finger tastes the meat — the mouth receives none; cauldrons stained — a greedy tongue aches in the belly.
101101.comment: 伏《坎》。艮为指，坎为肉，兑为口，震为鼎，鼎兑为舌，离为腹。《左传》："子公染指于鼎，尝之而出"，林似指其事。一当作以。

101110.poem: 言无要约，不成券契。殷叔季姬，公孙争之。强人委禽，不悦于心。
101110.poemEn: Words without compact — no deed or contract stands; Yin Shu and Lady Ji — the duke’s grandson contends; the strong man drops the prey — displeased at heart.
101110.comment: 正反兑相背故曰言无要约，不成券契。《左传昭元年》："郑徐吾犯之妹美，公孙楚聘之矣，公孙黑强委禽焉"。伏震为姬、为公，艮为季孙，正反艮故曰争。艮为禽，兑悦，伏坎为心。○殷叔未详，或徐吾犯出自殷。

101111.poem: 长女三嫁，进退无羞。牝狐作妖，夜行离忧。
101111.poemEn: The eldest daughter marries thrice — advancing and withdrawing without shame; a vixen works mischief — roaming by night, breeding care.
101111.comment: 巽为长女，伏震为嫁，数三，故曰三嫁。巽为进退，坤为羞，坤伏故无羞。伏坎为狐、为妖、为夜、为忧，巽为牝。○无羞，各本皆作多态，依《观》之《蛊》校。

110000.poem: 大斧斫木，谗人败国。东关二五，祸及三子。晋人乱危，怀公出走。
110000.poemEn: Great axes fell the timber — slanderers wreck the state; at East Gate at two and five — disaster strikes the three sons; Jin in chaos and peril — Duke Huai flees.
110000.comment: 兑为斧，震为木，兑震为口、为言，故曰谗人。坤为国、为关，兑数十，故曰二五。《左传僖二十八年》："姬赂外嬖梁五与东关嬖五"是也。震数三，故曰三子，申生、夷吾、重耳也。震为晋、为人、为公，坤为祸乱、为心，故曰怀公。○斫，宋元本作破，依汲古。

110001.poem: 庭燎夜明，追古伤今。阳弱不制，阴雄坐戾。
110001.poemEn: Court torches blaze by night — recalling the past and wounding the present; yang weak and not in control — yin swells and sits defiant.
110001.comment: 详《剥》之《大有》。

110010.poem: 文王四乳，仁爱笃厚。子畜十男，夭折无有。
110010.poemEn: King Wen with four nipples — benevolence deep and thick; ten sons reared — none die young.
110010.comment: 震为王，伏离，故曰文王。艮为乳，震卦数四，故曰四乳。震为仁爱，艮为笃厚，震为子，兑数十，故曰十男。兑为折，震生故不折。《帝王世纪》："文王身长十尺有四乳"，《诗》："大姒嗣徽音，则百斯男"，《传》："太姒十子"，据《史记索隐》注十子"伯邑考、武王、管、蔡、霍、鲁、卫、毛、聃、曹"是也。○夭，元本作发，音跋，《周礼》有赤犮氏，注：赤犮，犹捇拔除去之也，亦可通，兹依宋本、汲古，惟各本皆作无有夭折，依《鼎》之《蒙》校，有厚为韵。

110011.poem: 熊罴豹狼，在山阴阳。伺鹿取獐，道畏难。
110011.poemEn: Bears, leopards, wolves — on the mountains in shade and sun; watching for deer and taking roe — the road is feared and hard.
110011.comment: 二至五正反艮故曰熊罴豹狼。艮纳丙故曰山阳，艮反则山阴矣，故曰山阴。易《中孚》："鸣鹤在阴"，亦山阴也，解者皆误。艮止故曰伺，艮手故曰取。震鹿艮麞。，斥也，掌检行道路伺候盗贼。○，汲古作伏，非，依宋元本。

110100.poem: 亡羊东泽，循堤直北。子思其母，复返其所。
110100.poemEn: Lose sheep at the eastern marsh — along the dike we go straight north; the son longs for his mother — and returns to his place.
110100.comment: 兑为羊、为泽，震东故曰东泽，震往故曰亡羊。坎为北，震为阪，故曰循堤直北。震为子，坎为思，巽为母，巽伏故思母。震为归，故复返其所。○复，汲古作随，依宋元本。

110101.poem: 缺囊破筐，空无黍粱。不媚如公，弃于粪墙。
110101.poemEn: A torn purse and broken basket — empty of millet and grain; not apt to flatter like the lord — thrown down by the dung wall.
110101.comment: 此用《颐》象。坤为囊，震为筐，伏兑毁，故曰缺、曰破。震为稻粱、为黍稷，坤虚故曰空。震为公，兑为媚，兑伏故曰不媚。艮为墙，坤柔，故曰粪墙。○粱，元本作稷，依汲古。

110110.poem: 鼻顶移徙，居不安坐。枯竹复生，失其宠荣。
110110.poemEn: Nose-bridge shifted and moved — dwellings ill at ease; a dry bamboo shoots again — favor and honor are lost.
110110.comment: 伏艮为鼻、为顶，互震故曰移徙。艮为居、为坐，震动故不安坐。震为竹，离科上槁，故曰枯竹。震为复、为生，艮阳在上为宠荣，互坎故失其宠荣。坎为失也。○顶，汲古作项，复作后，依宋元本。居，宋元本作君，依汲古。

110111.poem: 蜂虿之门，难以止息。嘉媚之士，为王所食。从去其室。
110111.poemEn: A gate of bees and scorpions — hard to rest within; a pleasing gentleman — devoured by the king; so we leave the house.
110111.comment: 巽为虫，伏坎为毒，故曰蜂虿。乾为门，风散故难以止息。兑为媚、为食，乾为王，伏坎为室，言王食养嘉士，士皆归王室也。伏震为士。○门，汲古作国，今依宋元本。

111000.poem: 被狐乘龙，为王道东。过时不返，使我忧聋。
111000.poemEn: Clad like a fox and riding a dragon — eastward on the king’s road; time passes without return — my worry grows deaf.
111000.comment: 伏艮为狐，震为龙，言被狐裘乘龙马也。震为道、为东，乾为王，震往故不返。坤为忧，坤迷故聋。○被，宋元本作放，依汲古。

111001.poem: 谗以内安，不利其国。室家大惧，幽囚重闭。疾病多求，罪乱愦愦。
111001.poemEn: Slander kept within to quiet — not good for the state; households in great fear — shut in heavy confinement; sickness with many pleas — guilt and chaos confused.
111001.comment: 三至上正反震，故曰谗。艮为国、为室家，伏坤为惧、为幽闭、为重、为疾病、为罪乱，言内有谗人，群臣被谗，幽囚重闭，不利其国也。坤迷故曰愦愦。○谗，宋元本作说，利作离，大惧作相欢，均依汲古。

111010.poem: 履危无患，跳脱独全。不利出门，伤我左膝。疾病不食，鬼哭其室。
111010.poemEn: Treading peril without harm — leaping free, I alone am whole; not good to go out — my left knee is hurt; sick and not eating — ghosts weep in the house.
111010.comment: 坎为危、为患，跳脱在外故无患。乾为门户，出门遇险故不利。兑为伤膝象，疑为坎股之屈信全在膝，而坎为矫輮，又为美脊，以义、以形皆有膝象。互离为东，故曰伤我左膝。坎为病，兑为食，坎忧，故云不食。坎为鬼、为室，兑为口，故曰鬼哭其室也。○跳，汲古作逃，依宋元本。膝，宋元本作踝，今依汲古。

111011.poem: 六翮长翼，夜过射国。高飞冥冥，羿氏无得。
111011.poemEn: Six quills and long wings — by night we pass the land of archers; flying high into the dark — the house of Yi wins nothing.
111011.comment: 伏《豫》。震为翮、为翼，坎数六，故曰六翮长翼。坤为夜、为国，震为射，故曰射国。震为飞，坤恶，故曰羿，坤虚故无得。

111100.poem: 江海淮济，盈溢为害。邑被其濑，年困无岁。
111100.poemEn: Yangtze, sea, Huai, and Ji — floods harm the land; the town lashed by the current — the year bears no yield.
111100.comment: 乾为河、为盈，兑毁故曰害。伏坤为邑，乾为年岁。○济，宋元本作海，依汲古。

111101.poem: 轰轰，驰东逐西。盛盈必毁，高位崩颠。
111101.poemEn: Thunderous — racing east and chasing west; fullness must break — high stations topple and fall.
111101.comment: 此用遇卦象。震为车、为声，故曰轰。震为东、为驰逐，兑为西。乾为盛盈，兑为毁，故曰盛盈必毁。艮为高位，艮覆为震，故曰崩颠。○第二句宋元本作驱车东西，兹依汲古。

111110.poem: 嘉门福喜，缯帛盛炽。日就为得，财宝敌国。
111110.poemEn: A lucky gate and joy — silk and cloth piled high; day by day we win — treasure rich enough to rival states.
111110.comment: 乾为门、为福，兑悦故喜。伏坤为缯帛，乾为盛、为日、为财宝，伏坤为多，故曰敌国，言富可敌国。○喜，宋元本作善，依汲古。

111111.poem: 思初道古，哀吟无辅。阳明不制，上失其所。
111111.poemEn: Thinking of first ways and ancient — lamenting without support; bright yang not in command — those above lose their place.
111111.comment: 乾为初、为古，《颐》互坤为思、为哀，震为道、为吟，一阳在上故曰失所。阳明不制者，言阳不能制阴也。全用遇卦象。○道，元本作悼，依宋本、汲古。

000000.poem: 江河淮海，天之奥府。众利所聚，可以饶有，乐我君子。
000000.poemEn: Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and sea — Heaven’s deep storehouse; where all profits gather — abundance and plenty — delight for my gentleman.
000000.comment: 详《乾》之《观》。

010001.poem: 秋南春北，随时休息。处和履中，安无忧凶。
010001.poemEn: Autumn south, spring north — rest in season; dwelling in harmony and treading the mean — secure and free of harm.
010001.comment: 伏兑为秋，艮纳丙，故曰秋南。震为春，坤为北，故曰春北。艮为鸿雁，雁随阳转故曰随时。艮为时、为休息。坎为中和，震为履，艮为安。

010111.poem: 东家凶妇，怨其公姥。毁柈破盆，弃其饭飡，使吾困贫。
010111.poemEn: The eastern house’s fierce wife — she hates her elders; trays smashed and bowls broken — the meal thrown away; we are left poor and pinched.
010111.comment: 巽为妇，坎凶，伏震为东、为公，巽为姥。姥，母也。伏震为柈、为盆，坎为破，巽为饭飡，风散故曰弃。伏坤为吾、为贫。○怨，元本作怒，姥作姑，依宋本、汲古。柈，汲古作盘，依宋元本。

010000.poem: 泥滓污辱，弃捐沟渎。众所笑哭，终不显录。
010000.poemEn: Mud and sludge defile and shame — cast into the ditches; laughed and wept at by all — in the end none record you.
010000.comment: 坤土坎水故曰泥、曰污，坎为沟渎、为众，震为笑哭，坤贱坎隐，故曰终不显录。○污，宋元本作洿，依汲古。

000010.poem: 旦往暮还，各与相存，身无凶患。
000010.poemEn: Go at dawn, return at dusk — each tends the other; the body meets no mischance.
000010.comment: 《颐》震为旦、为往，坤为暮，艮者，震之反，故曰暮还。坤为身，坎为患。○凶患，汲古作患凶，依宋元本。

000111.poem: 雹梅零坠，心思愦愦，乱我魂气。
000111.poemEn: Hail and plum-blossoms fall — thoughts in confusion; my soul and breath disordered.
000111.comment: 乾艮皆为果，而乾为冰，故曰雹梅。《方言》："大裤谓之倒顿"，郭注：即今之雹裤。雹裤、雹梅皆象形语，巽陨故曰坠。坤为心，坤迷故曰愦愦。○汲古多"怀忧少愧"四字，在第三句，依宋元本。按：乾为魂，坤为乱，故曰乱我魂气。

001000.poem: 乘船涉济，载水逢火。赖得无患，蒙我生全。
001000.poemEn: By boat we ford the Ji — bearing water we meet fire; by good fortune no harm — our lives kept whole.
001000.comment: 震为船，坎为水、为济，艮为火，故曰载水逢火。坎为患，震为乐，故曰无患。○生全，汲古作全生，依宋元本。

000100.poem: 至德之君，政仁且温。伊吕股肱，国富民安。
000100.poemEn: A lord of utmost virtue — governance humane and mild; Yi and Lü as arms and thighs — the state rich and the people at ease.
000100.comment: 震为君、为仁，坤为政，艮为火，故曰政仁且温。伏巽为股肱，伊吾，语声。吕，从口，皆震象也。又艮为臣，亦或为艮象，坤为国、为民。○至德，汲古作德至，依宋元本。

011001.poem: 南历玉山，东入生门。登福上堂，饮万岁浆。
011001.poemEn: South past Jade Mountain — east through the Gate of Birth; up to the hall of blessing — we drink the long-life draught.
011001.comment: 震为南、为玉，艮山，故曰南历王山。艮门，震东，巽入，故东入生门。震为登、为福，艮为堂，故曰登福上堂。兑口为饮，兑泽故曰浆，震为万岁。

000011.poem: 一室百孙，公悦妪欢。相与笑言，家乐以安。
000011.poemEn: One house with a hundred grandsons — the lord delighted, the old woman glad; laughing and speaking together — the household at ease in joy.
000011.comment: 艮为室、为孙，坤为百，故曰一室百孙。巽为妪，伏震为公、为欢笑，艮为家。

000001.poem: 弱足刖跟，不利出门。商贾无赢，折崩为患。
000001.poemEn: Weak feet, heels cut — not fit to go out; merchants make no gain — collapse brings harm.
000001.comment: 汤火之忧，转解喜来。此用《颐》象。震为足、为跟，艮刀，故曰刖，坤柔，故曰弱，故出不利，坤为门也。震为商贾，上震覆故无赢、故崩折。坤为患、为水，艮火故曰汤火。○商，宋元本作市，崩作朋，皆非，依汲古。

011110.poem: 六龙俱怒，战于阪下。苍黄不胜，旅人艰苦。
011110.poemEn: Six dragons all in wrath — they battle at a slope’s foot; in panic they cannot prevail — the traveler suffers hardship.
011110.comment: 乾数六，故曰六龙。震为怒，《颐》正反震，故曰战。艮为阪，坤为下，震为苍黄、为旅人。皆用伏象。○阪，汲古作陂，苍作仓，均依宋元本。

010010.poem: 天下雷行，尘起不明。市空无羊，疾人忧凶。三木不辜，脱归家邦。
010010.poemEn: Thunder runs through the world — dust rises, things unclear; the market empty of sheep — the sick fear misfortune; yet the three woods are blameless — we slip free and return home.
010010.comment: 艮为天，震为雷，艮上震下，故曰天下雷行。艮为尘，坎黑故不明。兑为羊，巽为市，兑巽皆伏，故曰市空无羊。坎为疾、为忧，震为木，数三，故曰三木。三木，拲、桎、梏，亦坎象也。艮为家邦，震为脱，三木不辜，言虽被三木之刑而非其罪也。

001110.poem: 喜笑不常，失其福庆。口辟言疥，行者畏忌。
001110.poemEn: Smiles not kept — blessing and celebration lost; a mouth opened in rash words — travelers fear and shrink.
001110.comment: 兑为喜笑，正反兑故曰不常。乾为福庆，巽陨落故曰失。兑为口，乾为言，辟，邪也，疥，疮也，言口邪言秽也。伏坤为畏忌，艮为节，故曰疥。○辟，汲古作辨，依宋元本。疥，宋元本作，依汲古。

011100.poem: 毛生豪背，国乐民富。侯王有德。
011100.poemEn: Hair grows thick upon the back — the realm at ease, the people rich; lords and kings possess virtue.
011100.comment: 《山海经》：竹山有兽，状如豚，白毛，名曰豪彘。注：夹髀有麄毫，能以脊上毫射物，故曰毛生豪背。震为毛，伏艮为背、为国，坤为民、为富，乾为侯王。○豪，汲古作毫，依宋元本。

001111.poem: 豶豕童牛，害伤不来。三女同堂，生我福仁。
001111.poemEn: Castrated boar and young ox — harm does not come; three women share one hall — they bear me blessing and kindness.
001111.comment: 巽为豕，艮为牛，艮少，故曰豶豕童牛，象本《大畜》也。互巽为女，艮数三，艮为堂，故曰三女同堂。乾为福仁。伏震为生。○害，宋元本作童，依汲古。女，汲古作光，依宋元本。

000101.poem: 两虎争鬬，股创无处。不成仇雠，行解却去。
000101.poemEn: Two tigers fight — wounds on the thighs everywhere; hatred not formed — they break off and withdraw.
000101.comment: 详《大畜》之《损》。

001010.poem: 杀行桃园，见虎东还。螳螂之敌，使我无患。
001010.poemEn: On a killing march through the peach grove — seeing a tiger, I turn east; foes like a mantis — they do me no harm.
001010.comment: 此用《颐》象。震为行、为桃，艮为园、为虎，震为东、为反，故曰东还螳螂，疑伏兑象。《左传宣二年》："赵穿攻灵公于桃园，●之"，《淮南子》："齐庄公出行，有螳螂奋臂当车，回车避之"。○还，元本作西，使作仁，均依汲古。

010100.poem: 箕仁入室，政衰弊极。抱其彝器，奔于他国，因祸受福。
010100.poemEn: The humane of Ji enter the house — rule decays to extremity; clutching ritual vessels — they flee to another state; from harm they receive blessing.
010100.comment: 此用《颐》象。震为箕、为仁，艮为室，入室谓箕子囚于圜室也。坤为政、为弊，艮为抱，震为彝器、为奔，坤为国。抱其彝器，《周本纪》："少师强抱其祭器以犇周"，《宋世家》又云："微子持祭器造于军门"是也。○箕仁，元本作饥人，依宋本、汲古。黄丕烈从元本，非，因不知入室之义，而据《殷本纪》"西伯伐饥国"为说，然于下文义愈不协。

011111.poem: 执绥登车，骖乘东游。说齐解燕，霸国以安。
011111.poemEn: Taking reins I mount the car — as second driver I travel east; persuading Qi and unbinding Yan — the hegemon’s state finds peace.
011111.comment: 《史记苏秦传》："臣居燕不能使燕重，而在齐则燕重"，林用其事。巽为绥，伏震为车、为东、为燕、为解，巽为齐，伏坤为国，乾健故目［当作曰］霸国。

000110.poem: 水深无桴，蹇难何游。商伯失利，庶人愁忧。
000110.poemEn: Water deep without a raft — hindered and hard, how to go? The merchant-lord loses profit — common folk grieve.
000110.comment: 坤为水，震为桴，震伏故无桴，艮止故蹇。巽为利，坤丧故失利。坤为庶人、为忧。

011000.poem: 三鸟鸳鸯，相随俱行。南到饶泽，食鱼与粱。君子长乐，见恶不伤。
011000.poemEn: Three waterfowl and a pair of mandarin ducks — follow one another in flight; south to the rich marsh — they feed on fish and grain; the gentleman’s long joy — seeing ill yet not harmed.
011000.comment: 震为鸟，数三，故曰三鸟，坤文故曰鸳鸯。震为随、为行、为南，兑为泽，坤多，故曰饶泽。坤为鱼，震为粱，互兑，故曰食鱼与粱。伏艮为君子，坤为恶，震乐，故见恶不伤。○长乐，宋元本作乐长，依汲古。

010110.poem: 远视目盻，临深苦眩。不离越都，旅人留难。
010110.poemEn: Gazing far the eyes strain — at the brink the dizziness grows; we do not leave the Yue capital — the traveler is detained.

011010.poem: 终风东西，涣散四方。终日至暮，不见子欢。
011010.poemEn: Winds at the last, east and west — scattered to the four sides; all day till dusk — I do not see my child’s joy.

011101.poem: 牛马聋聩，不知声味。远贤贱仁，自令乱愦。
011101.poemEn: Ox and horse deaf and dull — they cannot know sound or taste; distance the worthy and cheapen humaneness — you bring on confusion.
011101.comment: 伏《屯》。坤牛、震马、坎耳，坤迷，故聋瞆。震为声，本卦巽为味，震为贤仁，在下故曰远贤贱仁。坤为贱、为乱。○各本下有"疾病无患，生福在门"八字，语意与上文不协，断为衍文，依《小过》之《谦》删。瞆，汲古作愦，依宋元本。令，宋元本作合，依汲古。

001001.poem: 据斗运枢，顺天无忧，与乐并居。艮为星，卦数七，故曰斗。
001001.poemEn: Set by the Dipper, pivot turning — follow Heaven without worry; dwelling together with joy.
001001.comment: 互坎为枢，艮为天，坤顺，卦二阴承一阳，故曰顺天坎忧。震乐故曰并居。

001011.poem: 姬奭姜望，为武守邦。屏藩燕齐，周室以强，子孙亿昌。
001011.poemEn: Ji Shi and Jiang Wang — guard the state for Wu; they screen Yan and Qi — the Zhou house grows strong; sons and grandsons flourish without end.
001011.comment: 伏震为姬、为奭，巽为姜，离为望，故曰姬奭姜望。震为武，艮为守、为邦、为屏藩，艮为燕，巽齐，言姬奭封燕，姜望封齐，屏藩周室，为武王守上也。震周坎室，震子艮孙。亿，大也。

001101.poem: 载船逢火，忧不为祸。家在山东，入门见公。
001101.poemEn: A boat meets fire — worry brings no disaster; home east of the mountains — on entering I see my lord.
001101.comment: 通《节》。震为船，艮为火，故曰载船逢火。坎为忧、为祸，船近水故虽逢火不为祸患。艮为家、为山，震为东，故曰家在山东。震为公，艮为门，巽入，故曰入门见公。

011011.poem: 绝国异路，心不相慕。蛇子两角，使我相恶。
011011.poemEn: Distant states and different roads — hearts do not yearn; a serpent’s young with two horns — make us hate each other.
011011.comment: 通《震》。艮为国、为路，坎为心、为慕，二至上两震相反，故不相慕。巽为蛇，伏艮为角，兑卦数二，故曰两角。《新序》："孙叔敖为儿时，出游，见两头蛇杀而埋之，归而泣"，林似指其事。○国，宋元本作言，依汲古。

010011.poem: 火息无光，年岁不长，殷商以亡。艮火在坎水上故无光。
010011.poemEn: Fire quenched with no light — the years do not last; Shang of Yin thereby perishes.
010011.comment: 震为年岁、为子，故曰殷商。子，殷姓也，坎失故曰亡。○殷商以亡，汲古作殷汤远明，元本作殷汤光明，而首句多殷商以亡一句。按：殷汤以亡，即殷汤远明，元本误为上句耳，宋本与汲古皆作三句可证。又年字汲古作千，依宋元本。

001100.poem: 凋叶被霜，独蔽不伤。驾入喜门，与福为婚。
001100.poemEn: Withered leaves struck by frost — one alone covered and unharmed; we drive through the gate of joy — wedding ourselves to blessing.
001100.comment: 震为叶，巽落故曰凋叶。艮为门，震为喜福，霜或用兑泽象，抑或取大坎。○凋，宋本、汲古作雕，依元本。

010101.poem: 顺风直北，与欢相得。岁熟年丰，邑无盗贼。
010101.poemEn: With fair wind straight north — we find our joy; harvests ripe and rich — no thieves in the town.
010101.comment: 似亦取《颐》象。

100000.poem: 牧羊稻园，闻虎呻喧。惧畏惕息，终无祸患。
100000.poemEn: Herding sheep by the rice fields — I hear a tiger groan; frightened, breath held — yet in the end no harm.
100000.comment: 坤为养、为牧，震为羊，震为稻，坤为园、为虎，震为喧，伏乾，乾惕故惧畏惕息。坤为祸，震乐，故无。○无，从宋元，汲古作免。

100001.poem: 冬华不实，国多盗贼。疾病难医，鬼哭其室。
100001.poemEn: Flowers in winter bear no fruit — the realm thick with thieves; sickness hard to heal — ghosts weep in their rooms.
100001.comment: 艮为果实，坤为冬，震为花，坤虚，故花而不实。坤为国，伏巽为盗，正反巽，故多盗。坤为疾病，坤死，故难医，坤为鬼，震为哭，艮为室，故曰鬼哭其室。

100010.poem: 兵征大宛，北出玉关。与胡寇战，平城道西，七日绝粮，身几不全。
100010.poemEn: Troops march on Dayuan — north through the Jade Gate; we fight Hu raiders west of Pingcheng Road — seven days without grain, bodies nearly not whole.
100010.comment: 坎众、坤众，故曰兵。震为征，坎位西，故曰大宛。艮为关，震为玉、为出，坤位北，故曰北出玉关。坤阴为胡，坎为寇，正覆艮震，故曰战。艮为城、为道，坎为平、为西，震数七，伏乾为日，震为粮，坤虚，故曰七日绝粮。坤为身、为死，故曰不全。《史记》：「高帝至平城，为匈奴所围，七日不得食」。大宛，西域国名，《史记》有《大宛传》。坎坤全用先天卦位。

100011.poem: 水载船舟，无根以浮。往来溶溶，心劳且忧。
100011.poemEn: Water bears the boats — rootless they float; drifting to and fro — the heart labors and worries.
100011.comment: 坤为水，震为船，坤为载，巽下断，在水上故曰无根以浮。震为往，又为反，故曰往来，坤水，故曰溶溶。伏大坎为心、为劳、为忧。○载，宋、汲古误戴，从元本。

100100.poem: 龟鳖列市，河海饶有。长财善贾，商季悦喜。
100100.poemEn: Turtle and tortoise rank the market — river and sea abound; long capital, skillful traders — the merchant’s youngest rejoices.
100100.comment: 互艮为龟鳖，伏巽为市。坎为河海，坎众，故曰饶有。伏巽为利、为长、为商贾，艮为季，震为列、为善，又为悦喜。○财，宋元本皆作钱，贾作价，均依汲古。

100101.poem: 陈妫敬仲，兆兴齐姜。营邱是适，八世大昌。
100101.poemEn: Chen Gui and Jingzhong — an omen of Qi Jiang’s rise; to Yingqiu they go — eight generations greatly prosper.
100101.comment: 震为陈，坎为仲，艮为笃敬，故曰敬仲。坎为兆，伏巽为齐、为姜，互艮为营邱，震往，故曰适。艮为世，数八，震为昌。妫，陈姓，敬仲，即公子完。庄二十二年奔齐，初懿氏卜妻，敬仲曰：「有妫之后，将育于姜」，故曰兆兴齐姜。

100110.poem: 太乙驾骝，从天上来。徵我叔季，封为鲁侯，无有凶忧。
100110.poemEn: Taiyi drives a dappled steed — descending from Heaven; he summons my uncles — enfeoffed as marquises of Lu — no dread of harm.
100110.comment: 太乙，星名，即北辰也。艮为星，震为马，艮在震上，故曰驾骝。否上之初，故曰从天上来。艮为叔季、为求，故曰徵我叔季。兑为鲁，震为侯，故曰鲁侯。坎为忧，震乐，故无有凶忧。○宋元本无第五句，依汲古。

100111.poem: 鸣条之灾，北奔犬胡。左祍为长，国号匈奴。主君旄头，立尊单于。
100111.poemEn: The disaster of Mingtiao — north to the Dog Hu they flee; the Left Worthy made chief — the nation named Xiongnu; the hair banner of the lord — he is set up as Chanyu.
100111.comment: 震为鸣、为木，故曰鸣条。乾伏坤位北，坤又为胡，艮犬，故曰北奔犬胡。震为祍、为左、为长，《论语》：「吾其被发左祍」，胡俗也。艮为国、为奴仆，震为号，故曰国号匈奴。震为主，乾为君、为头，震为多发，故曰主君旄头。震为立，艮为尊，乾君故曰单于，《史记》：「汤伐桀于鸣条」，又《匈奴传》索隐引乐彦《括地谱》云：「汤放桀鸣条，其子獯粥妻桀之众妾，避居北野，随畜移徙」，中国谓之匈奴。旄头，被发也。《汉官仪》：「旧选羽林为旄头，被发先驱」是其证。由林词观之，《括地谱》之说与古故实合。○灾，宋元本作图，依汲古。

101000.poem: 虿室蜂户，螫我手足。不可进取，为身害速。
101000.poemEn: A scorpion room, a bee-gate — they sting hands and feet; press not forward — harm to the body comes swift.
101000.comment: 此用遇卦屯象。坎为室、为毒，坤为户，伏巽为虫，故曰虿室蜂户。坎为棘、为刺、为螫，艮为手，震为足、为进取，坤凶，故不可进取，坤为身、为害，震为速。○速，从宋元本，汲古等本多作咎，与足不韵。

101001.poem: 路多枳棘，步刺我足。不利旅客，为心作毒。
101001.poemEn: Roads thick with thorns — the step pricks my feet; ill for a traveler — poison born in the heart.
101001.comment: 艮震为道路，坎为枳棘、为刺，震为步、为足、为旅客，坎险故不利，坎为心、为毒。

101010.poem: 栋隆辅强，宠贵日光。福善并作，乐以高明。
101010.poemEn: Beams swelling and buttresses strong — favor and honor bright as the sun; blessing and goodness together — delight in high brightness.
101010.comment: 此用屯象。坎为极、为栋、为车、为辅，《大过》「栋桡之凶，不可以有辅也」，《诗》「勿弃尔辅」，《毛传》「辅以佐车」。辅，夹车木也。坎在上，故曰栋隆，艮坚，故曰辅强。艮为日、为光、为宠贵，震为福善、为乐，艮为高明。

101011.poem: 崔嵬北岳，天神贵客。温仁正直，主布恩德。闵哀不已，蒙受大福。
101011.poemEn: Lofty North Mountain — heaven’s spirits honored as guests; warm, humane, and upright — the lord spreads grace; pity unending — great blessing received.
101011.comment: 此用《屯》象。坎北艮山，故曰北岳。震为神、为仁、为客，坎为忧，故曰闵哀。震为恩德、为大福。○闵哀，宋元本、汲古本皆作开衣，非，依局本。闵哀不已者，言悲悯人世，予人以福也。

101100.poem: 黄鸟悲鸣，愁不见星。困于鸷鸟，鸇使我惊。
101100.poemEn: Yellow birds cry in sorrow — no stars to be seen; oppressed by hawks — the goshawk startles me.
101100.comment: 震为黄、为鸟、为鸣，互大坎，故悲鸣，故愁。离为星，坎伏，故不见。伏艮为鸷鸟、为鸇，坎为困，震为鸷。○下二句依宋元本，汲古作「困于鸷鸇、使我心惊」。又元本困讹因。

101101.poem: 阴变为阳，女化作男。治道得通，君臣相承。
101101.poemEn: Yin turns to yang — the woman becomes a man; the way of rule is cleared — lord and ministers continue each other.
101101.comment: 通《坎》。乾二五之坤成坎，坎为中男、为阳卦，故阴化阳、女作男。坎中爻艮为道路、为臣，震为君，故曰君臣相承。《五行志》：「魏襄王十三年，有女子化为丈夫。」

101110.poem: 从容长闲，游戏南山。拜祠祷神，神使无患。
101110.poemEn: Leisure and long ease — we sport on South Mountain; bowing, praying, and offering — the spirits spare us harm.
